concept.title: Parity-Preserving Self-Reduction for Assembly Counting
concept.concept_description:
The complementation bijection is witness-preserving, so it should transport not only solvability but every modular counting class. The conjecture is that P to its complement is a parsimonious self-reduction, making the mod-2 assembly count a complementation invariant while the exact count stays #P-hard.

For every framed puzzle P, the assembly counts of P and of its complement are equal, and the map P to compPuzzle P is a polynomial-time parsimonious self-reduction of the assembly counting problem.

Combine assemblyEquiv with the piece-count encoding of the catalog reduction and formalise a counting-reduction predicate; check the mod-2 invariance on enumerated small instances.

Modular counting for jigsaw assembly inherits all hardness of modular SAT counting, with complementation as a free symmetry of the instance space.

The encoding, not the mathematics, breaks parsimony, indicating that piece multiplicities carry counting information.

/-!
# Parity-preserving self-reduction for jigsaw assembly counting — the model

A *framed jigsaw puzzle on `n` variables* consists of `n` variable sockets, each of
which receives one of two variable pieces (tab = `1`, blank = `0`), together with a
list of clause pieces.  A clause piece exposes finitely many literal inputs, each
milled for a socket `i : Fin n` and a polarity `p : ZMod 2`; it snaps into place iff
at least one of its inputs mates with the variable piece chosen at its socket.

We work over `ZMod 2` so that global tab–blank complementation becomes the
translation `p ↦ p + 1`, and the whole symmetry group of the instance space is the
*hyperoctahedral group* `(ZMod 2)^n ⋊ Sₙ` of signed permutations of the sockets.

## Main results

* `SignedPerm.assemblyEquiv` : every signed permutation `g` induces an explicit
  bijection between the assembly space of `P` and that of `g • P`.
* `SignedPerm.count_actPuzzle` : the assembly count is an invariant of the whole
  hyperoctahedral action (not only of global complementation).
* `SignedPerm.actPuzzle_mul` : the action on puzzles is compatible with the group
  law of signed permutations, so invariance holds along whole orbits.
* `count_compPuzzle`, `count_compPuzzle_modEq`, `even_count_compPuzzle_iff` :
  global complementation is parsimonious; in particular every modular count, and
  the mod-2 count, is a complementation invariant.
* `compPuzzle_eq_self_iff` : complementation acts *freely* on the instance space
  away from the degenerate puzzles all of whose clause pieces are empty.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace JigsawParsimony

open Finset

/-- The Boolean cube of variable-piece choices, written additively over `ZMod 2`. -/
abbrev Cube (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ZMod 2

/-- A literal input of a clause piece: a socket together with the polarity it is
milled for. -/
abbrev Lit (n : ℕ) := Fin n × ZMod 2

/-- A clause piece, given by its list of literal inputs. -/
abbrev ClausePiece (n : ℕ) := List (Lit n)

/-- A framed puzzle on `n` variables: its list of clause pieces. -/
abbrev Puzzle (n : ℕ) := List (ClausePiece n)

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- A literal input mates with the variable piece chosen at its socket. -/
def Fits (a : Cube n) (l : Lit n) : Prop := a l.1 = l.2

instance (a : Cube n) (l : Lit n) : Decidable (Fits a l) := by
  unfold Fits; infer_instance

/-- A choice of variable pieces assembles the puzzle when every clause piece has an
input that mates. -/
def Assembles (P : Puzzle n) (a : Cube n) : Prop := ∀ c ∈ P, ∃ l ∈ c, Fits a l

instance (P : Puzzle n) : DecidablePred (Assembles P) := by
  intro a; unfold Assembles; infer_instance

/-- The full (finite) assembly space of a puzzle. -/
def assemblies (P : Puzzle n) : Finset (Cube n) := univ.filter (Assembles P)

/-- The assembly count of a puzzle. -/
def count (P : Puzzle n) : ℕ := (assemblies P).card

@[simp] theorem mem_assemblies {P : Puzzle n} {a : Cube n} :
    a ∈ assemblies P ↔ Assembles P a := by
  simp [assemblies]

theorem count_eq_card_subtype (P : Puzzle n) :
    count P = Fintype.card {a : Cube n // Assembles P a} := by
  rw [Fintype.card_subtype]; rfl

/-! ## The hyperoctahedral group acting on puzzles -/

/-- A signed permutation of the sockets: relabel sockets by `perm`, then flip the
tab/blank polarity at socket `i` by `mask i`. -/
@[ext] structure SignedPerm (n : ℕ) where
  perm : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)
  mask : Cube n

namespace SignedPerm

variable (g h : SignedPerm n)

/-- Action on literal inputs. -/
def actLit (l : Lit n) : Lit n := (g.perm l.1, l.2 + g.mask l.1)

/-- Action on puzzles: transform every literal input of every clause piece. -/
def actPuzzle (P : Puzzle n) : Puzzle n := P.map (List.map g.actLit)

/-- Action on choices of variable pieces. -/
def actCube (a : Cube n) : Cube n := fun j => a (g.perm.symm j) + g.mask (g.perm.symm j)

/-- Inverse action on choices of variable pieces. -/
def invCube (b : Cube n) : Cube n := fun i => b (g.perm i) - g.mask i

theorem invCube_actCube (a : Cube n) : g.invCube (g.actCube a) = a := by
  funext i; simp [invCube, actCube]

theorem actCube_invCube (b : Cube n) : g.actCube (g.invCube b) = b := by
  funext j; simp [invCube, actCube]

theorem actCube_injective : Function.Injective g.actCube :=
  Function.LeftInverse.injective g.invCube_actCube

/-- Literal level transport. -/
theorem fits_act (a : Cube n) (l : Lit n) :
    Fits (g.actCube a) (g.actLit l) ↔ Fits a l := by
  simp only [Fits, actCube, actLit, Equiv.symm_apply_apply]
  exact add_left_inj _

/-- Puzzle level transport: `g` maps assemblies of `P` exactly onto assemblies of
`g • P`. -/
theorem assembles_act (P : Puzzle n) (a : Cube n) :
    Assembles (g.actPuzzle P) (g.actCube a) ↔ Assembles P a := by
  constructor
  · intro h c hc
    obtain ⟨l, hl, hf⟩ := h _ (List.mem_map_of_mem hc)
    obtain ⟨l', hl', rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 hl
    exact ⟨l', hl', (g.fits_act a l').1 hf⟩
  · intro h c hc
    obtain ⟨c', hc', rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 hc
    obtain ⟨l, hl, hf⟩ := h c' hc'
    exact ⟨g.actLit l, List.mem_map_of_mem hl, (g.fits_act a l).2 hf⟩

/-- **Witness-preserving bijection** induced by a signed permutation. -/
def assemblyEquiv (P : Puzzle n) :
    {a : Cube n // Assembles P a} ≃ {b : Cube n // Assembles (g.actPuzzle P) b} where
  toFun a := ⟨g.actCube a.1, (g.assembles_act P a.1).2 a.2⟩
  invFun b := ⟨g.invCube b.1, by
    have hb := b.2
    rw [← g.actCube_invCube b.1] at hb
    exact (g.assembles_act P _).1 hb⟩
  left_inv a := Subtype.ext (g.invCube_actCube a.1)
  right_inv b := Subtype.ext (g.actCube_invCube b.1)

/-- The assembly space of `g • P` is the image of that of `P`. -/
theorem assemblies_actPuzzle (P : Puzzle n) :
    assemblies (g.actPuzzle P) = (assemblies P).image g.actCube := by
  ext b
  simp only [mem_assemblies, Finset.mem_image]
  constructor
  · intro hb
    refine ⟨g.invCube b, ?_, g.actCube_invCube b⟩
    rw [← g.actCube_invCube b] at hb
    exact (g.assembles_act P _).1 hb
  · rintro ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩
    exact (g.assembles_act P a).2 ha

/-- **Hyperoctahedral invariance of the assembly count.** -/
theorem count_actPuzzle (P : Puzzle n) : count (g.actPuzzle P) = count P := by
  rw [count_eq_card_subtype, count_eq_card_subtype]
  exact (Fintype.card_congr (g.assemblyEquiv P)).symm

/-- Group law of signed permutations (`g * h` acts as "first `h`, then `g`"). -/
instance : Mul (SignedPerm n) :=
  ⟨fun g h => ⟨h.perm.trans g.perm, fun i => h.mask i + g.mask (h.perm i)⟩⟩

theorem mul_perm : (g * h).perm = h.perm.trans g.perm := rfl

theorem mul_mask (i : Fin n) : (g * h).mask i = h.mask i + g.mask (h.perm i) := rfl

theorem actLit_mul (l : Lit n) : (g * h).actLit l = g.actLit (h.actLit l) := by
  simp only [actLit, mul_perm, mul_mask, Equiv.trans_apply, Prod.mk.injEq, true_and]
  ring

/-- The action on puzzles is a genuine (left) action of the signed-permutation
monoid. -/
theorem actPuzzle_mul (P : Puzzle n) :
    (g * h).actPuzzle P = g.actPuzzle (h.actPuzzle P) := by
  simp only [actPuzzle, List.map_map]
  refine List.map_congr_left fun c _ => ?_
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, List.map_map]
  exact List.map_congr_left fun l _ => g.actLit_mul h l

/-- Orbit invariance: the count is constant along any finite word of signed
permutations. -/
theorem count_foldr_actPuzzle (gs : List (SignedPerm n)) (P : Puzzle n) :
    count (gs.foldr (fun g Q => g.actPuzzle Q) P) = count P := by
  induction gs with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons g gs ih => simp only [List.foldr_cons]; rw [count_actPuzzle, ih]

end SignedPerm

# Future Directions — Parsimonious Self-Reduction for Jigsaw Assembly Counting

## What this cycle established (Lean, 0 sorries)

* Complementation is one element of a parsimonious action of the whole hyperoctahedral
  group `(ZMod 2)^n ⋊ Sₙ` on framed puzzles (`SignedPerm.count_actPuzzle`,
  `SignedPerm.actPuzzle_mul`).  As a corollary every modular count, including the mod-2
  count, is a complementation invariant (`count_compPuzzle_modEq`).
* Complementation is a size-preserving, involutive parsimonious self-reduction of
  `#Jigsaw` (`compReduction`). `#SAT` (DIMACS) and `#Jigsaw` reduce parsimoniously to each
  other (`satToJigsaw`, `jigsawToSat`). Hardness transfer holds for every modular class
  (`reduction_to_jigsaw_of_reduction_to_sat`).
* Polarity-mask symmetries force 2-adic divisibility: `|maskSymm P| = 2^k` divides
  `count P` (`exists_two_pow_dvd_count`). This order is a hyperoctahedral invariant
  (`card_maskSymm_actPuzzle`), and odd counts force a trivial symmetry group
  (`maskSymm_eq_bot_of_odd`).
* The *encoding* breaks parsimony: labelled physical assemblies number
  `count P · (m+2)! · n! · n!` (`card_labeledAssembly`). That number is always even, and it is
  never parsimonious for a solvable puzzle (`labeled_not_parsimonious`).
* Mod-2 count via signless inclusion–exclusion over clause subsets (`count_cast_zmod_two`).

Boundary of the claims: "polynomial time" is modelled only by a linear bound on
encoding size; running time is not formalised.  #P-hardness itself is not formalised;
only the parsimonious transfer from `#SAT` is.

## Conjectures

### 1. Affine-subcube parity criterion
Each falsifier set in the mod-2 inclusion–exclusion formula is an affine subcube. So
`count P mod 2` should be the parity of the number of clause subsets `S` whose literal
inputs are consistent and pin *every* socket.
*The key insight is* that a falsifier set has cardinality `0` or `2^(n − |vars(S)|)`, so only
the full-pinning consistent subsets contribute.
*Why now?* `count_cast_zmod_two` reduces the claim to a single cardinality lemma about
falsifier sets.

module

public import Mathlib

/-!
# Parity-preserving self-reduction for jigsaw assembly counting — the model

A *framed jigsaw puzzle on `n` variables* consists of `n` variable sockets, each of
which receives one of two variable pieces (tab = `1`, blank = `0`), together with a
list of clause pieces.  A clause piece exposes finitely many literal inputs, each
milled for a socket `i : Fin n` and a polarity `p : ZMod 2`; it snaps into place iff
at least one of its inputs mates with the variable piece chosen at its socket.

We work over `ZMod 2` so that global tab–blank complementation becomes the
translation `p ↦ p + 1`, and the whole symmetry group of the instance space is the
*hyperoctahedral group* `(ZMod 2)^n ⋊ Sₙ` of signed permutations of the sockets.

## Main results

* `SignedPerm.assemblyEquiv` : every signed permutation `g` induces an explicit
  bijection between the assembly space of `P` and that of `g • P`.
* `SignedPerm.count_actPuzzle` : the assembly count is an invariant of the whole
  hyperoctahedral action (not only of global complementation).
* `SignedPerm.actPuzzle_mul` : the action on puzzles is compatible with the group
  law of signed permutations, so invariance holds along whole orbits.
* `count_compPuzzle`, `count_compPuzzle_modEq`, `even_count_compPuzzle_iff` :
  global complementation is parsimonious; in particular every modular count, and
  the mod-2 count, is a complementation invariant.
* `compPuzzle_eq_self_iff` : complementation acts *freely* on the instance space
  away from the degenerate puzzles all of whose clause pieces are empty.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace JigsawParsimony

open Finset

/-- The Boolean cube of variable-piece choices, written additively over `ZMod 2`. -/
abbrev Cube (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ZMod 2

/-- A literal input of a clause piece: a socket together with the polarity it is
milled for. -/
abbrev Lit (n : ℕ) := Fin n × ZMod 2

/-- A clause piece, given by its list of literal inputs. -/
abbrev ClausePiece (n : ℕ) := List (Lit n)

/-- A framed puzzle on `n` variables: its list of clause pieces. -/
abbrev Puzzle (n : ℕ) := List (ClausePiece n)

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- A literal input mates with the variable piece chosen at its socket. -/
def Fits (a : Cube n) (l : Lit n) : Prop := a l.1 = l.2

instance (a : Cube n) (l : Lit n) : Decidable (Fits a l) := by
  unfold Fits; infer_instance

/-- A choice of variable pieces assembles the puzzle when every clause piece has an
input that mates. -/
def Assembles (P : Puzzle n) (a : Cube n) : Prop := ∀ c ∈ P, ∃ l ∈ c, Fits a l

instance (P : Puzzle n) : DecidablePred (Assembles P) := by
  intro a; unfold Assembles; infer_instance

/-- The full (finite) assembly space of a puzzle. -/
def assemblies (P : Puzzle n) : Finset (Cube n) := univ.filter (Assembles P)

/-- The assembly count of a puzzle. -/
def count (P : Puzzle n) : ℕ := (assemblies P).card

@[simp] theorem mem_assemblies {P : Puzzle n} {a : Cube n} :
    a ∈ assemblies P ↔ Assembles P a := by
  simp [assemblies]

theorem count_eq_card_subtype (P : Puzzle n) :
    count P = Fintype.card {a : Cube n // Assembles P a} := by
  rw [Fintype.card_subtype]; rfl

/-! ## The hyperoctahedral group acting on puzzles -/

/-- A signed permutation of the sockets: relabel sockets by `perm`, then flip the
tab/blank polarity at socket `i` by `mask i`. -/
@[ext] structure SignedPerm (n : ℕ) where
  perm : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)
  mask : Cube n

namespace SignedPerm

variable (g h : SignedPerm n)

/-- Action on literal inputs. -/
def actLit (l : Lit n) : Lit n := (g.perm l.1, l.2 + g.mask l.1)

/-- Action on puzzles: transform every literal input of every clause piece. -/
def actPuzzle (P : Puzzle n) : Puzzle n := P.map (List.map g.actLit)

/-- Action on choices of variable pieces. -/
def actCube (a : Cube n) : Cube n := fun j => a (g.perm.symm j) + g.mask (g.perm.symm j)

/-- Inverse action on choices of variable pieces. -/
def invCube (b : Cube n) : Cube n := fun i => b (g.perm i) - g.mask i

theorem invCube_actCube (a : Cube n) : g.invCube (g.actCube a) = a := by
  funext i; simp [invCube, actCube]

theorem actCube_invCube (b : Cube n) : g.actCube (g.invCube b) = b := by
  funext j; simp [invCube, actCube]

theorem actCube_injective : Function.Injective g.actCube :=
  Function.LeftInverse.injective g.invCube_actCube

/-- Literal level transport. -/
theorem fits_act (a : Cube n) (l : Lit n) :
    Fits (g.actCube a) (g.actLit l) ↔ Fits a l := by
  simp only [Fits, actCube, actLit, Equiv.symm_apply_apply]
  exact add_left_inj _

/-- Puzzle level transport: `g` maps assemblies of `P` exactly onto assemblies of
`g • P`. -/
theorem assembles_act (P : Puzzle n) (a : Cube n) :
    Assembles (g.actPuzzle P) (g.actCube a) ↔ Assembles P a := by
  constructor
  · intro h c hc
    obtain ⟨l, hl, hf⟩ := h _ (List.mem_map_of_mem hc)
    obtain ⟨l', hl', rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 hl
    exact ⟨l', hl', (g.fits_act a l').1 hf⟩
  · intro h c hc
    obtain ⟨c', hc', rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 hc
    obtain ⟨l, hl, hf⟩ := h c' hc'
    exact ⟨g.actLit l, List.mem_map_of_mem hl, (g.fits_act a l).2 hf⟩

/-- **Witness-preserving bijection** induced by a signed permutation. -/
def assemblyEquiv (P : Puzzle n) :
    {a : Cube n // Assembles P a} ≃ {b : Cube n // Assembles (g.actPuzzle P) b} where
  toFun a := ⟨g.actCube a.1, (g.assembles_act P a.1).2 a.2⟩
  invFun b := ⟨g.invCube b.1, by
    have hb := b.2
    rw [← g.actCube_invCube b.1] at hb
    exact (g.assembles_act P _).1 hb⟩
  left_inv a := Subtype.ext (g.invCube_actCube a.1)
  right_inv b := Subtype.ext (g.actCube_invCube b.1)

/-- The assembly space of `g • P` is the image of that of `P`. -/
theorem assemblies_actPuzzle (P : Puzzle n) :
    assemblies (g.actPuzzle P) = (assemblies P).image g.actCube := by
  ext b
  simp only [mem_assemblies, Finset.mem_image]
  constructor
  · intro hb
    refine ⟨g.invCube b, ?_, g.actCube_invCube b⟩
    rw [← g.actCube_invCube b] at hb
    exact (g.assembles_act P _).1 hb
  · rintro ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩
    exact (g.assembles_act P a).2 ha

/-- **Hyperoctahedral invariance of the assembly count.** -/
theorem count_actPuzzle (P : Puzzle n) : count (g.actPuzzle P) = count P := by
  rw [count_eq_card_subtype, count_eq_card_subtype]
  exact (Fintype.card_congr (g.assemblyEquiv P)).symm

/-- Group law of signed permutations (`g * h` acts as "first `h`, then `g`"). -/
instance : Mul (SignedPerm n) :=
  ⟨fun g h => ⟨h.perm.trans g.perm, fun i => h.mask i + g.mask (h.perm i)⟩⟩

theorem mul_perm : (g * h).perm = h.perm.trans g.perm := rfl

theorem mul_mask (i : Fin n) : (g * h).mask i = h.mask i + g.mask (h.perm i) := rfl

theorem actLit_mul (l : Lit n) : (g * h).actLit l = g.actLit (h.actLit l) := by
  simp only [actLit, mul_perm, mul_mask, Equiv.trans_apply, Prod.mk.injEq, true_and]
  ring

/-- The action on puzzles is a genuine (left) action of the signed-permutation
monoid. -/
theorem actPuzzle_mul (P : Puzzle n) :
    (g * h).actPuzzle P = g.actPuzzle (h.actPuzzle P) := by
  simp only [actPuzzle, List.map_map]
  refine List.map_congr_left fun c _ => ?_
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, List.map_map]
  exact List.map_congr_left fun l _ => g.actLit_mul h l

/-- Orbit invariance: the count is constant along any finite word of signed
permutations. -/
theorem count_foldr_actPuzzle (gs : List (SignedPerm n)) (P : Puzzle n) :
    count (gs.foldr (fun g Q => g.actPuzzle Q) P) = count P := by
  induction gs with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons g gs ih => simp only [List.foldr_cons]; rw [count_actPuzzle, ih]

end SignedPerm

/-! ## Global tab–blank complementation -/

/-- Global complementation of a puzzle: reverse the polarity of every literal
input. -/
def compPuzzle (P : Puzzle n) : Puzzle n := P.map (List.map fun l => (l.1, l.2 + 1))

/-- Global complementation of a choice of variable pieces. -/
def compCube (a : Cube n) : Cube n := fun i => a i + 1

/-- Complementation is the signed permutation with trivial relabelling and full
mask. -/
def compSigned (n : ℕ) : SignedPerm n := ⟨1, fun _ => 1⟩

theorem compPuzzle_eq_actPuzzle (P : Puzzle n) :
    compPuzzle P = (compSigned n).actPuzzle P := rfl

theorem compCube_eq_actCube (a : Cube n) : compCube a = (compSigned n).actCube a := rfl

theorem add_one_add_one_zmod2 (x : ZMod 2) : x + 1 + 1 = x := by
  rw [add_assoc]; fin_cases x <;> rfl

theorem compPuzzle_involutive : Function.Involutive (compPuzzle (n := n)) := by
  intro P
  simp only [compPuzzle, List.map_map]
  conv_rhs => rw [← List.map_id P]
  refine List.map_congr_left fun c _ => ?_
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, List.map_map, id]
  conv_rhs => rw [← List.map_id c]
  refine List.map_congr_left fun l _ => ?_
  simp [add_one_add_one_zmod2]

theorem compCube_involutive : Function.Involutive (compCube (n := n)) := by
  intro a; funext i; simp [compCube, add_one_add_one_zmod2]

/-- The witness-preserving complementation bijection `assemblyEquiv`. -/
def assemblyEquiv (P : Puzzle n) :
    {a : Cube n // Assembles P a} ≃ {b : Cube n // Assembles (compPuzzle P) b} :=
  (compSigned n).assemblyEquiv P

/-- **Parsimony of complementation.**  `P` and its complement have equal assembly
counts. -/
theorem count_compPuzzle (P : Puzzle n) : count (compPuzzle P) = count P :=
  (compSigned n).count_actPuzzle P

/-- Every modular counting class is a complementation invariant. -/
theorem count_compPuzzle_modEq (k : ℕ) (P : Puzzle n) :
    count (compPuzzle P) ≡ count P [MOD k] := by
  rw [count_compPuzzle]

/-- The mod-2 assembly count is a complementation invariant. -/
theorem even_count_compPuzzle_iff (P : Puzzle n) :
    Even (count (compPuzzle P)) ↔ Even (count P) := by
  rw [count_compPuzzle]

/-- A clause piece is fixed by complementation only if it has no inputs. -/
theorem compClause_eq_self_iff (c : ClausePiece n) :
    c.map (fun l => (l.1, l.2 + 1)) = c ↔ c = [] := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    cases c with
    | nil => rfl
    | cons l c =>
        exfalso
        have h1 := (List.cons.inj h).1
        have h2 : l.2 + 1 = l.2 := congrArg Prod.snd h1
        have : (1 : ZMod 2) = 0 := by
          have := congrArg (fun x => x - l.2) h2
          simp at this
        exact absurd this (by decide)
  · rintro rfl; rfl

/-- **Freeness on the instance space.**  A puzzle is its own complement exactly
when all its clause pieces are empty; on every other instance complementation
moves the instance. -/
theorem compPuzzle_eq_self_iff (P : Puzzle n) :
    compPuzzle P = P ↔ ∀ c ∈ P, c = [] := by
  induction P with
  | nil => simp [compPuzzle]
  | cons c P ih =>
      simp only [compPuzzle, List.map_cons, List.cons.injEq, List.mem_cons,
        forall_eq_or_imp] at ih ⊢
      rw [compClause_eq_self_iff, ih]

/-- The degenerate self-complementary puzzles have count `0` (if some clause piece
is present) or `2^n` (the empty puzzle). -/
theorem count_of_compPuzzle_eq_self (P : Puzzle n) (h : compPuzzle P = P) :
    count P = if P = [] then 2 ^ n else 0 := by
  rw [compPuzzle_eq_self_iff] at h
  split_ifs with hP
  · subst hP
    rw [count, assemblies, Finset.filter_true_of_mem (fun a _ c hc => by simp at hc)]
    simp
  · obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := List.exists_mem_of_ne_nil P hP
    have hc0 := h c hc
    subst hc0
    rw [count, Finset.card_eq_zero, Finset.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]
    intro a ha
    obtain ⟨l, hl, _⟩ := (mem_assemblies.1 ha) [] hc
    simp at hl

end JigsawParsimony

module

public import Catalog.Algebra.JigsawParsimony.Basic

/-!
# The encoding, not the mathematics, breaks parsimony

The abstract assembly count (`count`) counts *choices of variable pieces*.  A
physical jigsaw solver, however, places *labelled* physical pieces into slots, and
the piece-count encoding of the SAT reduction uses many physically identical
pieces: `2` corner pieces and `m` clause pieces of one boundary shape (here called
`frame`), `n` identical tab variable pieces and `n` identical blank variable pieces,
for `2n + m + 2` pieces in total.

A *labelled assembly* is an abstract assembly together with a shape-preserving
relabelling of the physical pieces.  We prove:

* `card_relabel_eq_prod` (general multiplicity law) : for an arbitrary shape map,
  the number of shape-preserving relabellings is `∏ (multiplicity)!`, and it is `1`
  exactly when the shape map is injective (`prod_factorial_eq_one_iff`).
* `card_labeledAssembly` : for the SAT encoding,
  `#labelled = count P · (m+2)! · n! · n!`.
* `even_card_labeledAssembly` : the labelled count is always even, so it carries no
  mod-2 information at all, whereas `count` can be odd (`labeled_parity_collapse`).
* `labeled_not_parsimonious` : labelled counting is parsimonious for *no* solvable
  puzzle — piece multiplicities, not complementation, are what break parsimony.
* `count_eq_card_labeled_div` : the exact count is recovered by dividing out the
  multiplicity factor, so the multiplicities carry exactly the lost counting data.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace JigsawParsimony

open Finset

/-! ## General multiplicity law -/

theorem card_subtype_sum {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] (p : α ⊕ β → Prop)
    [DecidablePred p] :
    Fintype.card {x // p x} =
      Fintype.card {a // p (Sum.inl a)} + Fintype.card {b // p (Sum.inr b)} := by
  rw [← Fintype.card_sum]
  exact Fintype.card_congr Equiv.subtypeSum

/-- Number of shape-preserving relabellings of a finite set of pieces. -/
theorem card_relabel_eq_prod {α ι : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq ι]
    [Fintype ι] (f : α → ι) :
    Fintype.card {g : Equiv.Perm α // f ∘ g = f} = ∏ i, (Fintype.card {a // f a = i}).factorial :=
  DomMulAct.stabilizer_card f

/-- The multiplicity factor is trivial exactly when no two pieces share a shape. -/
theorem prod_factorial_eq_one_iff {α ι : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι]
    (f : α → ι) :
    ∏ i, (Fintype.card {a // f a = i}).factorial = 1 ↔ Function.Injective f := by
  rw [Finset.prod_eq_one_iff_of_one_le'
    (fun i _ => Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.2 (Nat.factorial_ne_zero _))]
  simp only [Finset.mem_univ, true_implies, Nat.factorial_eq_one]
  constructor
  · intro h x y hxy
    exact congrArg Subtype.val (Fintype.card_le_one_iff.1 (h (f y)) ⟨x, hxy⟩ ⟨y, rfl⟩)
  · intro hf i
    exact Fintype.card_le_one_iff.2 fun a b => Subtype.ext (hf (a.2.trans b.2.symm))

/-! ## The physical pieces of the SAT encoding -/

/-- Physical piece shapes used by the encoding. -/
inductive PieceShape
  | frame
  | tabVar
  | blankVar
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- Physical slots: `m + 2` frame-shaped pieces (two corners and `m` clause pieces),
`n` tab variable pieces, and `n` blank variable pieces. -/
abbrev Slot (n m : ℕ) := Fin (m + 2) ⊕ Fin n ⊕ Fin n

/-- The shape of the physical piece in each slot. -/
def slotShape {n m : ℕ} : Slot n m → PieceShape :=
  Sum.elim (fun _ => .frame) (Sum.elim (fun _ => .tabVar) (fun _ => .blankVar))

/-- The encoding uses exactly `2n + m + 2` physical pieces. -/
theorem card_slot (n m : ℕ) : Fintype.card (Slot n m) = 2 * n + m + 2 := by
  simp only [Fintype.card_sum, Fintype.card_fin]; ring

theorem card_frame (n m : ℕ) :
    Fintype.card {a : Slot n m // slotShape a = .frame} = m + 2 := by
  rw [card_subtype_sum, card_subtype_sum]; simp [slotShape]

theorem card_tabVar (n m : ℕ) :
    Fintype.card {a : Slot n m // slotShape a = .tabVar} = n := by
  rw [card_subtype_sum, card_subtype_sum]; simp [slotShape]

theorem card_blankVar (n m : ℕ) :
    Fintype.card {a : Slot n m // slotShape a = .blankVar} = n := by
  rw [card_subtype_sum, card_subtype_sum]; simp [slotShape]

/-- Shape-preserving relabellings of the physical pieces. -/
abbrev Relabel (n m : ℕ) := {g : Equiv.Perm (Slot n m) // slotShape ∘ g = slotShape}

/-- **Multiplicity factor of the encoding.** -/
theorem card_relabel (n m : ℕ) :
    Fintype.card (Relabel n m) = (m + 2).factorial * n.factorial * n.factorial := by
  rw [card_relabel_eq_prod, Fintype.prod_eq_mul_prod_compl PieceShape.frame]
  have hcompl : ({PieceShape.frame}ᶜ : Finset PieceShape) = {.tabVar, .blankVar} := by decide
  rw [hcompl, Finset.prod_pair (by decide), card_frame, card_tabVar, card_blankVar, mul_assoc]

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- A labelled assembly: an abstract assembly together with a shape-preserving
relabelling of the `2n + m + 2` physical pieces. -/
abbrev LabeledAssembly (P : Puzzle n) := {a : Cube n // Assembles P a} × Relabel n P.length

/-- **Labelled count = abstract count × multiplicity factor.** -/
theorem card_labeledAssembly (P : Puzzle n) :
    Fintype.card (LabeledAssembly P) =
      count P * ((P.length + 2).factorial * n.factorial * n.factorial) := by
  rw [Fintype.card_prod, card_relabel, ← count_eq_card_subtype]

/-- The labelled count is always even: it erases the mod-2 count. -/
theorem even_card_labeledAssembly (P : Puzzle n) : Even (Fintype.card (LabeledAssembly P)) := by
  rw [card_labeledAssembly]
  have h2 : 2 ∣ (P.length + 2).factorial := Nat.dvd_factorial (by norm_num) (by omega)
  exact even_iff_two_dvd.2 (Dvd.dvd.mul_left (Dvd.dvd.mul_right (Dvd.dvd.mul_right h2 _) _) _)

/-- Labelled counting is parsimonious for **no** solvable puzzle. -/
theorem labeled_not_parsimonious (P : Puzzle n) (hP : 0 < count P) :
    Fintype.card (LabeledAssembly P) ≠ count P := by
  rw [card_labeledAssembly]
  intro h
  have hf : (P.length + 2).factorial * n.factorial * n.factorial = 1 := by
    have := Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_left hP (h.trans (mul_one _).symm)
    exact this
  have h2 : 2 ≤ (P.length + 2).factorial := by
    calc 2 = (2 : ℕ).factorial := rfl
      _ ≤ (P.length + 2).factorial := Nat.factorial_le (by omega)
  have : (P.length + 2).factorial ≤ 1 := by
    rw [← hf, mul_assoc]
    exact Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (Nat.mul_pos (Nat.factorial_pos _) (Nat.factorial_pos _))
  omega

/-- The multiplicities carry exactly the lost counting information: dividing them
out recovers the abstract count. -/
theorem count_eq_card_labeled_div (P : Puzzle n) :
    count P = Fintype.card (LabeledAssembly P) /
      ((P.length + 2).factorial * n.factorial * n.factorial) := by
  rw [card_labeledAssembly, Nat.mul_div_cancel _ (by positivity)]

/-- The shape map of the encoding is never injective, so by the general
multiplicity law it can never be parsimonious. -/
theorem slotShape_not_injective (m : ℕ) : ¬ Function.Injective (slotShape (n := n) (m := m)) := by
  intro h
  have := h (a₁ := Sum.inl 0) (a₂ := Sum.inl 1) rfl
  exact absurd (Sum.inl.inj this) (by simp)

/-- **Parity collapse.**  On one variable, the unit clause `x₀` has an odd abstract
count, and its complement too (complementation preserves parity), yet both labelled
counts are even. -/
theorem labeled_parity_collapse :
    let P : Puzzle 1 := [[(0, 1)]]
    count P = 1 ∧ count (compPuzzle P) = 1 ∧
      Even (Fintype.card (LabeledAssembly P)) ∧
      Even (Fintype.card (LabeledAssembly (compPuzzle P))) := by
  intro P
  have h1 : count P = 1 := by decide
  exact ⟨h1, (count_compPuzzle P).trans h1, even_card_labeledAssembly P,
    even_card_labeledAssembly _⟩

end JigsawParsimony

/-!
# Enumerated small instances

Exhaustive kernel-checked experiments on the family `puzzlesN n` of all framed
puzzles with exactly two clause pieces whose inputs form a sublist of the `2n`
possible literal inputs (`256` puzzles for `n = 2`, `4096` for `n = 3`).

These finite checks *support* the general theorems of the sibling files; none of
the general theorems depends on them.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace JigsawParsimony

/-- All `2n` literal inputs on `n` sockets. -/
def litsN (n : ℕ) : List (Lit n) := (List.finRange n).flatMap fun i => [(i, 0), (i, 1)]

/-- All two-clause puzzles whose clause pieces are sublists of `litsN n`. -/
def puzzlesN (n : ℕ) : List (Puzzle n) :=
  let cs := (litsN n).sublists
  cs.flatMap fun c => cs.map fun d => [c, d]

theorem length_puzzlesN_two : (puzzlesN 2).length = 256 := by decide +kernel

/-- Exhaustive check (n = 2): complementation preserves the exact count. -/
theorem puzzlesN_two_comp_count :
    (puzzlesN 2).all (fun P => count (compPuzzle P) == count P) = true := by decide +kernel

/-- Exhaustive check (n = 3, 4096 puzzles): complementation preserves the count. -/
theorem puzzlesN_three_comp_count :
    (puzzlesN 3).all (fun P => count (compPuzzle P) == count P) = true := by decide +kernel

/-- Mod-2 invariance on the enumerated family, derived from the general theorem
(no enumeration needed). -/
theorem puzzlesN_comp_parity (n : ℕ) :
    ∀ P ∈ puzzlesN n, count (compPuzzle P) % 2 = count P % 2 := by
  intro P _
  exact count_compPuzzle_modEq 2 P

/-- Count histogram for `n = 2`: `35, 24, 88, 60, 49` puzzles have count
`0, 1, 2, 3, 4`; in particular `84` have odd count. -/
theorem puzzlesN_two_histogram :
    ((puzzlesN 2).map count).count 0 = 35 ∧ ((puzzlesN 2).map count).count 1 = 24 ∧
      ((puzzlesN 2).map count).count 2 = 88 ∧ ((puzzlesN 2).map count).count 3 = 60 ∧
      ((puzzlesN 2).map count).count 4 = 49 := by
  decide +kernel

/-- Exactly `88` of the `256` puzzles are self-dual in the assembly-space sense,
and all of them have even count — as `even_count_of_selfDual` predicts. -/
theorem puzzlesN_two_selfDual :
    ((puzzlesN 2).filter fun P => assemblies (compPuzzle P) == assemblies P).length = 88 ∧
      ((puzzlesN 2).filter fun P => assemblies (compPuzzle P) == assemblies P).all
        (fun P => count P % 2 == 0) = true := by
  decide +kernel

/-! ## A tight 2-adic example -/

/-- `(x₀ ∨ x₁) ∧ (¬x₀ ∨ ¬x₁)` on three sockets: `x₀ ≠ x₁`, `x₂` free. -/
def xorPuzzle : Puzzle 3 := [[(0, 1), (1, 1)], [(0, 0), (1, 0)]]

theorem count_xorPuzzle : count xorPuzzle = 4 := by decide +kernel

/-- The masks `(1,1,0)` and `(0,0,1)` are mask symmetries of `xorPuzzle`. -/
theorem xorPuzzle_masks :
    (![1, 1, 0] : Cube 3) ∈ maskSymm xorPuzzle ∧ (![0, 0, 1] : Cube 3) ∈ maskSymm xorPuzzle := by
  simp only [mem_maskSymm]
  constructor <;> decide +kernel

/-- `xorPuzzle` is self-dual (the all-ones mask is the sum of the two masks above),
so its count is even by the general theorem. -/
theorem xorPuzzle_selfDual : assemblies (compPuzzle xorPuzzle) = assemblies xorPuzzle := by
  decide +kernel

example : Even (count xorPuzzle) := even_count_of_selfDual (by norm_num) _ xorPuzzle_selfDual

/-- The labelled (physical) count of `xorPuzzle`: `4 · 4! · 3! · 3! = 3456`. -/
theorem card_labeled_xorPuzzle : Fintype.card (LabeledAssembly xorPuzzle) = 3456 := by
  rw [card_labeledAssembly, count_xorPuzzle]
  simp [xorPuzzle, Nat.factorial]

/-- The mod-2 inclusion–exclusion terms of `xorPuzzle`: `8 + 2 + 2 + 0 = 12`, which
is `≡ 4 = count xorPuzzle (mod 2)`. -/
theorem xorPuzzle_falsifierSum :
    ∑ S ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin xorPuzzle.length)).powerset, falsifierCount xorPuzzle S
      = 12 := by
  decide +kernel

example : count xorPuzzle ≡ 12 [MOD 2] :=
  xorPuzzle_falsifierSum ▸ count_modEq_falsifierSum xorPuzzle

/-! ## The DIMACS bridge on a concrete instance -/

/-- `(x₁ ∨ ¬x₂) ∧ (x₂ ∨ x₉)` on two declared variables (`x₉` is undeclared). -/
def demoCNF : DimacsCNF := ⟨2, [[1, -2], [2, 9]]⟩

theorem satCount_demoCNF : satCount demoCNF = 1 := by
  rw [← count_toPuzzle]; decide +kernel

end JigsawParsimony

module

public import Catalog.Algebra.JigsawParsimony.Basic

/-!
# Polarity-mask symmetries force 2-adic divisibility of the assembly count

Global complementation is one element (the all-ones mask) of the elementary abelian
2-group `Cube n = (ZMod 2)^n` of polarity masks.  For a puzzle `P` we form its
*mask-symmetry group* `maskSymm P`: the masks `s` such that flipping the variable
pieces by `s` never changes whether the puzzle assembles.  It is an additive
subgroup of `(ZMod 2)^n`, so its order is a power of two, and it acts freely by
translation on the assembly space.

## Main results

* `card_dvd_card_of_stable` : (Lagrange for stable sets) a finite set stable under
  translation by a subgroup `H` of a finite abelian group is a union of cosets, so
  `|H|` divides its cardinality.
* `card_maskSymm_dvd_count` : `|maskSymm P|` divides the assembly count.
* `exists_two_pow_dvd_count` : that order is `2^k` with `k ≤ n`, so the assembly
  count is divisible by `2^k`.
* `selfDual_iff_one_mem_maskSymm` : a puzzle has the same assembly space as its
  complement iff the all-ones mask is a mask symmetry.
* `even_count_of_selfDual` : such self-dual puzzles on `n ≥ 1` variables have an
  even assembly count.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace JigsawParsimony

open Finset

/-- **Lagrange for stable sets.**  If a finite set `S` in a finite abelian group is
stable under translation by the subgroup `H`, then `|H|` divides `|S|`: `S` is
partitioned into the cosets it meets, each of size `|H|`. -/
theorem card_dvd_card_of_stable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (H : AddSubgroup V) (S : Finset V) (hS : ∀ x ∈ S, ∀ h ∈ H, x + h ∈ S) :
    Nat.card H ∣ S.card := by
  classical
  let q : V → V ⧸ H := QuotientAddGroup.mk
  have hfib : ∀ b ∈ S.image q, (S.filter fun a => q a = b).card = Nat.card H := by
    intro b hb
    obtain ⟨x0, hx0, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hb
    have hset : (S.filter fun a => q a = q x0) =
        (univ.filter fun h => h ∈ H).image (fun h => x0 + h) := by
      ext a
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, q]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨_, hq⟩
        have hmem : -a + x0 ∈ H := QuotientAddGroup.eq.1 hq
        refine ⟨-x0 + a, ?_, by abel⟩
        have := H.neg_mem hmem
        simpa [neg_add, add_comm] using this
      · rintro ⟨h, hh, rfl⟩
        refine ⟨hS x0 hx0 h hh, ?_⟩
        apply QuotientAddGroup.eq.2
        have : -(x0 + h) + x0 = -h := by abel
        rw [this]
        exact H.neg_mem hh
    rw [hset, Finset.card_image_of_injective _ (add_right_injective x0),
      Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, Fintype.card_subtype]
  rw [Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise (f := q) (t := S.image q)
      (fun x hx => Finset.mem_coe.2 (Finset.mem_image_of_mem q (Finset.mem_coe.1 hx))),
    Finset.sum_const_nat hfib]
  exact Dvd.intro_left _ rfl

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- The mask-symmetry group of a puzzle: polarity masks whose translation action
preserves assemblability. -/
def maskSymm (P : Puzzle n) : AddSubgroup (Cube n) where
  carrier := {s | ∀ a, Assembles P (a + s) ↔ Assembles P a}
  zero_mem' := by intro a; simp
  add_mem' := by
    intro s t hs ht a
    rw [← add_assoc]
    exact (ht (a + s)).trans (hs a)
  neg_mem' := by
    intro s hs a
    have := hs (a + -s)
    rw [neg_add_cancel_right] at this
    exact this.symm

theorem mem_maskSymm {P : Puzzle n} {s : Cube n} :
    s ∈ maskSymm P ↔ ∀ a, Assembles P (a + s) ↔ Assembles P a := Iff.rfl

/-- **Mask symmetries divide the count.** -/
theorem card_maskSymm_dvd_count (P : Puzzle n) : Nat.card (maskSymm P) ∣ count P := by
  apply card_dvd_card_of_stable
  intro x hx h hh
  rw [mem_assemblies] at hx ⊢
  exact (hh x).2 hx

/-- The mask-symmetry group is a 2-group of order `2^k`, `k ≤ n`. -/
theorem card_maskSymm_eq_two_pow (P : Puzzle n) :
    ∃ k ≤ n, Nat.card (maskSymm P) = 2 ^ k := by
  have hdvd : Nat.card (maskSymm P) ∣ 2 ^ n := by
    have := (maskSymm P).card_addSubgroup_dvd_card
    simpa [Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, ZMod.card] using this
  exact (Nat.dvd_prime_pow Nat.prime_two).1 hdvd

/-- **2-adic divisibility.**  The assembly count is divisible by the order `2^k` of
the mask-symmetry group. -/
theorem exists_two_pow_dvd_count (P : Puzzle n) :
    ∃ k ≤ n, Nat.card (maskSymm P) = 2 ^ k ∧ 2 ^ k ∣ count P := by
  obtain ⟨k, hk, hcard⟩ := card_maskSymm_eq_two_pow P
  exact ⟨k, hk, hcard, hcard ▸ card_maskSymm_dvd_count P⟩

/-- The all-ones mask, i.e. global complementation of variable pieces. -/
def onesMask (n : ℕ) : Cube n := fun _ => 1

theorem compCube_eq_add_ones (a : Cube n) : compCube a = a + onesMask n := rfl

/-- Assembling the complement at `a + 1` is assembling `P` at `a`. -/
theorem assembles_compPuzzle_add_ones (P : Puzzle n) (a : Cube n) :
    Assembles (compPuzzle P) (a + onesMask n) ↔ Assembles P a := by
  have := (compSigned n).assembles_act P a
  rw [← compPuzzle_eq_actPuzzle, ← compCube_eq_actCube] at this
  exact this

/-- **Self-duality as a mask symmetry.**  `P` and its complement have the same
assembly space iff the all-ones mask lies in `maskSymm P`. -/
theorem selfDual_iff_one_mem_maskSymm (P : Puzzle n) :
    assemblies (compPuzzle P) = assemblies P ↔ onesMask n ∈ maskSymm P := by
  constructor
  · intro h a
    have h1 : Assembles (compPuzzle P) (a + onesMask n) ↔ Assembles P (a + onesMask n) := by
      rw [← mem_assemblies, ← mem_assemblies, h]
    exact h1.symm.trans (assembles_compPuzzle_add_ones P a)
  · intro h
    ext b
    rw [mem_assemblies, mem_assemblies]
    have hb : b = (b + onesMask n) + onesMask n := by
      funext i; simp [onesMask, add_one_add_one_zmod2]
    rw [hb, assembles_compPuzzle_add_ones]
    exact (h (b + onesMask n)).symm

theorem onesMask_ne_zero (hn : 0 < n) : onesMask n ≠ 0 := by
  intro h
  have h1 : (1 : ZMod 2) = 0 := congrFun h ⟨0, hn⟩
  exact absurd h1 (by decide)

/-- **Self-dual puzzles have even count.**  Recovered here as the `k = 1` case of
2-adic divisibility by the mask-symmetry group. -/
theorem even_count_of_selfDual (hn : 0 < n) (P : Puzzle n)
    (h : assemblies (compPuzzle P) = assemblies P) : Even (count P) := by
  rw [selfDual_iff_one_mem_maskSymm] at h
  obtain ⟨k, -, hcard, hdvd⟩ := exists_two_pow_dvd_count P
  have htwo : 1 < Nat.card (maskSymm P) := by
    refine Finite.one_lt_card_iff_nontrivial.2 ⟨⟨0, (maskSymm P).zero_mem⟩, ⟨onesMask n, h⟩,
      fun e => onesMask_ne_zero hn (congrArg Subtype.val e).symm⟩
  have hk : 1 ≤ k := by
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos k with rfl | hk
    · rw [pow_zero] at hcard; omega
    · exact hk
  exact even_iff_two_dvd.2 (dvd_trans (dvd_pow_self 2 (by omega)) hdvd)

/-- **Odd counts forbid polarity symmetry.**  A puzzle with an odd assembly count
has trivial mask-symmetry group. -/
theorem maskSymm_eq_bot_of_odd (P : Puzzle n) (h : Odd (count P)) : maskSymm P = ⊥ := by
  obtain ⟨k, -, hcard, hdvd⟩ := exists_two_pow_dvd_count P
  have hk : k = 0 := by
    by_contra hk
    have : 2 ∣ count P := dvd_trans (dvd_pow_self 2 hk) hdvd
    exact (Nat.not_even_iff_odd.2 h) (even_iff_two_dvd.2 this)
  subst hk
  rw [pow_zero] at hcard
  exact (AddSubgroup.card_eq_one).1 hcard

/-- Inverse transport of assemblability along a signed permutation. -/
theorem SignedPerm.assembles_actPuzzle_iff (g : SignedPerm n) (P : Puzzle n) (b : Cube n) :
    Assembles (g.actPuzzle P) b ↔ Assembles P (g.invCube b) := by
  conv_lhs => rw [← g.actCube_invCube b]
  exact g.assembles_act P _

theorem SignedPerm.invCube_add (g : SignedPerm n) (b s : Cube n) :
    g.invCube (b + s) = g.invCube b + s ∘ g.perm := by
  funext i
  simp only [SignedPerm.invCube, Pi.add_apply, Function.comp_apply]
  ring

/-- **Conjugation law.**  A mask `s` is a symmetry of `g • P` iff the relabelled mask
`s ∘ g.perm` is a symmetry of `P`. -/
theorem mem_maskSymm_actPuzzle (g : SignedPerm n) (P : Puzzle n) (s : Cube n) :
    s ∈ maskSymm (g.actPuzzle P) ↔ s ∘ g.perm ∈ maskSymm P := by
  simp only [mem_maskSymm, g.assembles_actPuzzle_iff, g.invCube_add]
  constructor
  · intro h a
    have := h (g.actCube a)
    rwa [g.invCube_actCube] at this
  · intro h b
    exact h (g.invCube b)

/-- **The order of the mask-symmetry group is a hyperoctahedral invariant**, so the
2-adic divisibility certificate of `count` is constant on orbits. -/
theorem card_maskSymm_actPuzzle (g : SignedPerm n) (P : Puzzle n) :
    Nat.card (maskSymm (g.actPuzzle P)) = Nat.card (maskSymm P) := by
  refine Nat.card_congr
    { toFun := fun s => ⟨s.1 ∘ g.perm, (mem_maskSymm_actPuzzle g P s.1).1 s.2⟩
      invFun := fun t => ⟨t.1 ∘ g.perm.symm, (mem_maskSymm_actPuzzle g P _).2 (by
        have : t.1 ∘ g.perm.symm ∘ g.perm = t.1 := by
          funext i; simp
        rw [Function.comp_assoc, this]; exact t.2)⟩
      left_inv := fun s => Subtype.ext (by funext i; simp)
      right_inv := fun t => Subtype.ext (by funext i; simp) }

/-- Complementation preserves the mask-symmetry group itself. -/
theorem maskSymm_compPuzzle (P : Puzzle n) : maskSymm (compPuzzle P) = maskSymm P := by
  ext s
  rw [compPuzzle_eq_actPuzzle, mem_maskSymm_actPuzzle]
  rfl

end JigsawParsimony

module

public import Catalog.Algebra.JigsawParsimony.Basic

/-!
# A mod-2 inclusion–exclusion formula for the assembly count

Over `ZMod 2` the indicator that a clause piece fits is `1 + [the piece is
falsified]`, so expanding the product over clause pieces yields an inclusion–
exclusion formula with no signs:

`count P ≡ ∑_{S ⊆ clause pieces} #{a : a falsifies every piece in S}  (mod 2)`.

Combined with `count_compPuzzle`, the falsifier sums of `P` and of its complement
agree mod 2 (`falsifierSum_compPuzzle`).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace JigsawParsimony

open Finset

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- A choice of variable pieces *falsifies* a clause piece when none of its inputs
mates. -/
def Falsifies (a : Cube n) (c : ClausePiece n) : Prop := ∀ l ∈ c, ¬ Fits a l

instance (a : Cube n) (c : ClausePiece n) : Decidable (Falsifies a c) := by
  unfold Falsifies; infer_instance

/-- Number of choices of variable pieces falsifying every clause piece indexed by
`S`. -/
def falsifierCount (P : Puzzle n) (S : Finset (Fin P.length)) : ℕ :=
  (univ.filter fun a : Cube n => ∀ i ∈ S, Falsifies a (P.get i)).card

theorem assembles_iff_forall_get (P : Puzzle n) (a : Cube n) :
    Assembles P a ↔ ∀ i : Fin P.length, ¬ Falsifies a (P.get i) := by
  unfold Assembles Falsifies
  simp only [not_forall, not_not, exists_prop]
  constructor
  · intro h i
    exact h _ (List.get_mem P i)
  · intro h c hc
    obtain ⟨i, rfl⟩ := List.get_of_mem hc
    exact h i

theorem fits_indicator (p : Prop) [Decidable p] :
    ((if ¬ p then 1 else 0 : ZMod 2)) = 1 + (if p then 1 else 0) := by
  by_cases hp : p <;> simp [hp]
  decide

/-- **Signless inclusion–exclusion mod 2.** -/
theorem count_cast_zmod_two (P : Puzzle n) :
    (count P : ZMod 2) = ∑ S ∈ (univ : Finset (Fin P.length)).powerset,
      (falsifierCount P S : ZMod 2) := by
  have h1 : (count P : ZMod 2) =
      ∑ a : Cube n, ∏ i : Fin P.length, (if ¬ Falsifies a (P.get i) then 1 else 0 : ZMod 2) := by
    rw [count, assemblies, ← Finset.sum_boole]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
    rw [Finset.prod_boole]
    simp only [Finset.mem_univ, true_implies, assembles_iff_forall_get]
  rw [h1]
  simp_rw [fits_indicator, Finset.prod_one_add, Finset.prod_boole]
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun S _ => ?_
  rw [falsifierCount, Finset.natCast_card_filter]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
  congr 1

/-- The same formula as a congruence of natural numbers. -/
theorem count_modEq_falsifierSum (P : Puzzle n) :
    count P ≡ ∑ S ∈ (univ : Finset (Fin P.length)).powerset, falsifierCount P S [MOD 2] := by
  rw [← ZMod.natCast_eq_natCast_iff, count_cast_zmod_two, Nat.cast_sum]

theorem length_compPuzzle (P : Puzzle n) : (compPuzzle P).length = P.length := by
  simp [compPuzzle]

/-- **Complementation invariance of the falsifier sum mod 2**: a nontrivial identity
between two inclusion–exclusion expansions, obtained from parsimony. -/
theorem falsifierSum_compPuzzle (P : Puzzle n) :
    ∑ S ∈ (univ : Finset (Fin (compPuzzle P).length)).powerset, falsifierCount (compPuzzle P) S
      ≡ ∑ S ∈ (univ : Finset (Fin P.length)).powerset, falsifierCount P S [MOD 2] :=
  ((count_modEq_falsifierSum (compPuzzle P)).symm.trans
    (by rw [count_compPuzzle])).trans (count_modEq_falsifierSum P)

end JigsawParsimony

module

public import Catalog.Algebra.JigsawParsimony.Basic

/-!
# Parsimonious counting reductions: `#SAT → #Jigsaw → #Jigsaw`

We formalise a *counting problem* (instances, an encoding size, and a count) and a
*parsimonious reduction* between counting problems: an instance map preserving the
exact count and blowing up the encoding size at most linearly.  (Linear size
growth is the formal proxy used here for "polynomial-time"; the maps below are
structural recursions over lists, but running time itself is not modelled.)

## Main results

* `ParsimoniousReduction.comp`, `ParsimoniousReduction.count_modEq` : parsimonious
  reductions compose and transport every modular count (`⊕P`, `Mod_kP`).
* `compReduction` / `compPuzzle_isParsimoniousSelfReduction` : global complementation
  is a size-preserving, involutive parsimonious self-reduction of `#Jigsaw`.
* `count_toPuzzle` : the encoding of DIMACS CNF formulas as framed puzzles preserves
  the number of solutions exactly (literals naming undeclared variables are
  genuinely unsatisfiable on both sides), giving `satToJigsaw`.
* `toDimacs`, `satCount_toDimacs` : the converse encoding, so `#SAT` and `#Jigsaw` are
  parsimoniously inter-reducible; `satToJigsawComp` composes with complementation.
* `reduction_to_jigsaw_of_reduction_to_sat` : every counting problem that reduces
  parsimoniously to `#SAT` reduces parsimoniously to `#Jigsaw`, through either `P`
  or its complement.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace JigsawParsimony

open Finset

/-- A counting problem: instances with an encoding size and a solution count. -/
structure CountingProblem where
  Inst : Type
  size : Inst → ℕ
  count : Inst → ℕ

/-- A parsimonious reduction with linearly bounded size growth. -/
structure ParsimoniousReduction (A B : CountingProblem) where
  map : A.Inst → B.Inst
  count_map : ∀ x, B.count (map x) = A.count x
  sizeMul : ℕ
  sizeAdd : ℕ
  size_map : ∀ x, B.size (map x) ≤ sizeMul * A.size x + sizeAdd

namespace ParsimoniousReduction

variable {A B C : CountingProblem}

/-- The identity reduction. -/
def refl (A : CountingProblem) : ParsimoniousReduction A A :=
  ⟨id, fun _ => rfl, 1, 0, fun x => by simp⟩

/-- Composition of parsimonious reductions. -/
def comp (g : ParsimoniousReduction B C) (f : ParsimoniousReduction A B) :
    ParsimoniousReduction A C where
  map := g.map ∘ f.map
  count_map x := by simp [g.count_map, f.count_map]
  sizeMul := g.sizeMul * f.sizeMul
  sizeAdd := g.sizeMul * f.sizeAdd + g.sizeAdd
  size_map x := by
    have h1 := g.size_map (f.map x)
    have h2 := f.size_map x
    calc C.size (g.map (f.map x)) ≤ g.sizeMul * B.size (f.map x) + g.sizeAdd := h1
      _ ≤ g.sizeMul * (f.sizeMul * A.size x + f.sizeAdd) + g.sizeAdd := by gcongr
      _ = g.sizeMul * f.sizeMul * A.size x + (g.sizeMul * f.sizeAdd + g.sizeAdd) := by ring

/-- Parsimonious reductions transport every modular counting class. -/
theorem count_modEq (f : ParsimoniousReduction A B) (k : ℕ) (x : A.Inst) :
    B.count (f.map x) ≡ A.count x [MOD k] := by
  rw [f.count_map]

/-- In particular they transport the mod-2 count. -/
theorem even_count_iff (f : ParsimoniousReduction A B) (x : A.Inst) :
    Even (B.count (f.map x)) ↔ Even (A.count x) := by
  rw [f.count_map]

end ParsimoniousReduction

/-! ## The counting problem `#Jigsaw` and its complementation self-reduction -/

/-- Encoding size of a framed puzzle: sockets + literal inputs + clause pieces. -/
def puzzleSize {n : ℕ} (P : Puzzle n) : ℕ := n + (P.map List.length).sum + P.length

/-- The assembly counting problem for framed jigsaw puzzles. -/
def jigsawCount : CountingProblem where
  Inst := Σ n : ℕ, Puzzle n
  size x := puzzleSize x.2
  count x := count x.2

theorem puzzleSize_compPuzzle {n : ℕ} (P : Puzzle n) :
    puzzleSize (compPuzzle P) = puzzleSize P := by
  simp [puzzleSize, compPuzzle, Function.comp_def]

/-- Complementation on instances of `#Jigsaw`. -/
def compInst (x : jigsawCount.Inst) : jigsawCount.Inst := ⟨x.1, compPuzzle x.2⟩

/-- **Complementation is a parsimonious self-reduction of `#Jigsaw`**, with no size
growth at all. -/
def compReduction : ParsimoniousReduction jigsawCount jigsawCount where
  map := compInst
  count_map x := count_compPuzzle x.2
  sizeMul := 1
  sizeAdd := 0
  size_map x := by simp [jigsawCount, compInst, puzzleSize_compPuzzle]

theorem compReduction_involutive : Function.Involutive compReduction.map := by
  rintro ⟨n, P⟩
  simp [compReduction, compInst, compPuzzle_involutive P]

/-- A self-map of an instance space is a *parsimonious self-reduction* if it
preserves the count and grows the size at most linearly. -/
def IsParsimoniousSelfReduction (A : CountingProblem) (f : A.Inst → A.Inst) : Prop :=
  (∀ x, A.count (f x) = A.count x) ∧ ∃ c d : ℕ, ∀ x, A.size (f x) ≤ c * A.size x + d

theorem compPuzzle_isParsimoniousSelfReduction :
    IsParsimoniousSelfReduction jigsawCount compInst :=
  ⟨compReduction.count_map, 1, 0, compReduction.size_map⟩

/-- Every signed permutation of the sockets gives a parsimonious self-reduction too. -/
theorem signedPerm_isParsimoniousSelfReduction
    (g : ∀ n, SignedPerm n) :
    IsParsimoniousSelfReduction jigsawCount (fun x => ⟨x.1, (g x.1).actPuzzle x.2⟩) := by
  refine ⟨fun x => (g x.1).count_actPuzzle x.2, 1, 0, fun x => ?_⟩
  simp [jigsawCount, puzzleSize, SignedPerm.actPuzzle, Function.comp_def]

/-! ## `#SAT` in DIMACS format -/

/-- A CNF formula in DIMACS style: `nvars` declared variables, literals are nonzero
integers `±(i+1)`. -/
structure DimacsCNF where
  nvars : ℕ
  clauses : List (List ℤ)

/-- Polarity of a DIMACS literal as an element of `ZMod 2`. -/
def dimacsPol (k : ℤ) : ZMod 2 := if 0 < k then 1 else 0

/-- A DIMACS literal is true under `a` if it names a declared variable carrying the
right polarity.  Literals naming undeclared variables (or `0`) are false. -/
def DimacsLitTrue {nv : ℕ} (a : Cube nv) (k : ℤ) : Prop :=
  ∃ i : Fin nv, k.natAbs = i.1 + 1 ∧ a i = dimacsPol k

instance {nv : ℕ} (a : Cube nv) (k : ℤ) : Decidable (DimacsLitTrue a k) := by
  unfold DimacsLitTrue; infer_instance

/-- Satisfaction of a DIMACS formula. -/
def DimacsCNF.Sat (F : DimacsCNF) (a : Cube F.nvars) : Prop :=
  ∀ c ∈ F.clauses, ∃ k ∈ c, DimacsLitTrue a k

instance (F : DimacsCNF) : DecidablePred F.Sat := by
  intro a; unfold DimacsCNF.Sat; infer_instance

/-- The number of satisfying assignments of the declared variables. -/
def satCount (F : DimacsCNF) : ℕ := (univ.filter F.Sat).card

/-- Encoding size of a DIMACS formula. -/
def dimacsSize (F : DimacsCNF) : ℕ := F.nvars + (F.clauses.map List.length).sum + F.clauses.length

/-- The counting problem `#SAT`. -/
def sharpSAT : CountingProblem := ⟨DimacsCNF, dimacsSize, satCount⟩

/-- Translate a DIMACS literal into a literal input milled for a declared socket,
discarding literals that name no declared variable. -/
def toLit (nv : ℕ) (k : ℤ) : Option (Lit nv) :=
  if h : k.natAbs - 1 < nv ∧ k ≠ 0 then some (⟨k.natAbs - 1, h.1⟩, dimacsPol k) else none

/-- The puzzle built from a DIMACS formula: one clause piece per clause. -/
def toPuzzle (F : DimacsCNF) : Puzzle F.nvars :=
  F.clauses.map (List.filterMap (toLit F.nvars))

theorem exists_toLit_fits_iff {nv : ℕ} (a : Cube nv) (k : ℤ) :
    (∃ l, toLit nv k = some l ∧ Fits a l) ↔ DimacsLitTrue a k := by
  unfold toLit DimacsLitTrue Fits
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨l, hl, hf⟩
    split_ifs at hl with h
    cases hl
    refine ⟨⟨k.natAbs - 1, h.1⟩, ?_, hf⟩
    have : k.natAbs ≠ 0 := Int.natAbs_ne_zero.2 h.2
    simp only
    omega
  · rintro ⟨i, hi, ha⟩
    have hk : k ≠ 0 := by
      intro hk; subst hk; simp at hi
    have hlt : k.natAbs - 1 < nv := by omega
    refine ⟨(⟨k.natAbs - 1, hlt⟩, dimacsPol k), by rw [dif_pos ⟨hlt, hk⟩], ?_⟩
    have : (⟨k.natAbs - 1, hlt⟩ : Fin nv) = i := Fin.ext (by simp only; omega)
    simpa [this] using ha

/-- The clause piece of `c` fits iff `c` is satisfied. -/
theorem clausePiece_fits_iff {nv : ℕ} (a : Cube nv) (c : List ℤ) :
    (∃ l ∈ c.filterMap (toLit nv), Fits a l) ↔ ∃ k ∈ c, DimacsLitTrue a k := by
  simp only [List.mem_filterMap]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨l, ⟨k, hk, hkl⟩, hf⟩
    exact ⟨k, hk, (exists_toLit_fits_iff a k).1 ⟨l, hkl, hf⟩⟩
  · rintro ⟨k, hk, ht⟩
    obtain ⟨l, hkl, hf⟩ := (exists_toLit_fits_iff a k).2 ht
    exact ⟨l, ⟨k, hk, hkl⟩, hf⟩

/-- **Witness-level correspondence.**  An assignment assembles the encoded puzzle
iff it satisfies the formula. -/
theorem assembles_toPuzzle_iff (F : DimacsCNF) (a : Cube F.nvars) :
    Assembles (toPuzzle F) a ↔ F.Sat a := by
  unfold Assembles toPuzzle DimacsCNF.Sat
  constructor
  · intro h c hc
    exact (clausePiece_fits_iff a c).1 (h _ (List.mem_map_of_mem hc))
  · intro h c hc
    obtain ⟨c', hc', rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 hc
    exact (clausePiece_fits_iff a c').2 (h c' hc')

/-- **Parsimony of the SAT-to-puzzle encoding.** -/
theorem count_toPuzzle (F : DimacsCNF) : count (toPuzzle F) = satCount F := by
  unfold count assemblies satCount
  congr 1
  ext a
  simp [assembles_toPuzzle_iff]

theorem length_filterMap_le {α β : Type*} (f : α → Option β) (l : List α) :
    (l.filterMap f).length ≤ l.length := by
  induction l with
  | nil => simp
  | cons x l ih =>
      rw [List.filterMap_cons]
      split <;> simp <;> omega

theorem puzzleSize_toPuzzle_le (F : DimacsCNF) : puzzleSize (toPuzzle F) ≤ dimacsSize F := by
  unfold puzzleSize dimacsSize toPuzzle
  simp only [List.map_map, List.length_map, add_le_add_iff_right, add_le_add_iff_left]
  apply List.sum_le_sum
  intro c _
  exact length_filterMap_le _ _

/-- The parsimonious reduction `#SAT → #Jigsaw`. -/
def satToJigsaw : ParsimoniousReduction sharpSAT jigsawCount where
  map F := ⟨F.nvars, toPuzzle F⟩
  count_map F := count_toPuzzle F
  sizeMul := 1
  sizeAdd := 0
  size_map F := by simpa [jigsawCount, sharpSAT] using puzzleSize_toPuzzle_le F

/-- `#SAT → #Jigsaw` followed by complementation: still parsimonious. -/
def satToJigsawComp : ParsimoniousReduction sharpSAT jigsawCount :=
  compReduction.comp satToJigsaw

/-! ## The converse encoding `#Jigsaw → #SAT` -/

/-- Encode a literal input as a DIMACS literal. -/
def litToDimacs {n : ℕ} (l : Lit n) : ℤ := if l.2 = 1 then (l.1.1 + 1 : ℤ) else -(l.1.1 + 1 : ℤ)

/-- Encode a framed puzzle as a DIMACS formula. -/
def toDimacs {n : ℕ} (P : Puzzle n) : DimacsCNF := ⟨n, P.map (List.map litToDimacs)⟩

theorem dimacsLitTrue_litToDimacs {n : ℕ} (a : Cube n) (l : Lit n) :
    DimacsLitTrue a (litToDimacs l) ↔ Fits a l := by
  obtain ⟨i, p⟩ := l
  have hp : p = 0 ∨ p = 1 := by fin_cases p <;> simp
  unfold DimacsLitTrue Fits litToDimacs dimacsPol
  rcases hp with rfl | rfl
  · simp only [zero_ne_one, if_false]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨j, hj, hja⟩
      have : j = i := Fin.ext (by omega)
      subst this
      simpa using hja
    · intro h
      refine ⟨i, by omega, ?_⟩
      simpa using h
  · simp only [if_true]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨j, hj, hja⟩
      have : j = i := Fin.ext (by omega)
      rw [this] at hja
      have hpos : (0 : ℤ) < (i.1 : ℤ) + 1 := by omega
      simpa [hpos] using hja
    · intro h
      refine ⟨i, by omega, ?_⟩
      have hpos : (0 : ℤ) < (i.1 : ℤ) + 1 := by omega
      simpa [hpos] using h

theorem sat_toDimacs_iff {n : ℕ} (P : Puzzle n) (a : Cube n) :
    (toDimacs P).Sat a ↔ Assembles P a := by
  unfold DimacsCNF.Sat toDimacs Assembles
  simp only [List.mem_map, forall_exists_index, and_imp, forall_apply_eq_imp_iff₂,
    exists_exists_and_eq_and, dimacsLitTrue_litToDimacs]

/-- **Parsimony of the puzzle-to-SAT encoding.** -/
theorem satCount_toDimacs {n : ℕ} (P : Puzzle n) : satCount (toDimacs P) = count P := by
  unfold count assemblies satCount
  congr 1
  ext a
  simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
  exact sat_toDimacs_iff P a

/-- The parsimonious reduction `#Jigsaw → #SAT`. -/
def jigsawToSat : ParsimoniousReduction jigsawCount sharpSAT where
  map x := toDimacs x.2
  count_map x := satCount_toDimacs x.2
  sizeMul := 1
  sizeAdd := 0
  size_map x := by
    simp [sharpSAT, jigsawCount, dimacsSize, puzzleSize, toDimacs, Function.comp_def]

/-- **Hardness transfer.**  Any counting problem parsimoniously reducible to `#SAT`
reduces parsimoniously to `#Jigsaw`; and the reduction can be post-composed with
complementation, so modular counts transfer through either `P` or its complement. -/
theorem reduction_to_jigsaw_of_reduction_to_sat {A : CountingProblem}
    (f : ParsimoniousReduction A sharpSAT) (k : ℕ) (x : A.Inst) :
    jigsawCount.count ((satToJigsaw.comp f).map x) ≡ A.count x [MOD k] ∧
      jigsawCount.count ((satToJigsawComp.comp f).map x) ≡ A.count x [MOD k] :=
  ⟨(satToJigsaw.comp f).count_modEq k x, (satToJigsawComp.comp f).count_modEq k x⟩

end JigsawParsimony

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Parity-Preserving Self-Reduction for Jigsaw Assembly Counting -- numerical demo.

A framed jigsaw puzzle on n sockets is a list of clause pieces; each clause piece is
a list of literal inputs (i, p) with i a socket in {0,...,n-1} and p a polarity in
{0,1} (0 = blank, 1 = tab).  A choice a in {0,1}^n of variable pieces *assembles*
the puzzle when every clause piece has an input (i, p) with a[i] == p.

This script checks, on exhaustively enumerated and random small instances:

  1. Signed-permutation (hyperoctahedral) invariance of the assembly count, via an
     explicit witness bijection.
  2. Compatibility of the action with the group law of signed permutations.
  3. Global complementation is a parsimonious, involutive, size-preserving
     self-reduction; every modular count is a complementation invariant.
  4. Complementation is free away from puzzles whose clause pieces are all empty.
  5. 2-adic divisibility: the polarity-mask symmetry group has order 2^k dividing
     the count; odd counts force a trivial symmetry group; the order is a
     hyperoctahedral invariant.
  6. The mod-2 count via signless inclusion-exclusion, and the affine-subcube
     criterion (only consistent, fully pinning clause subsets contribute).
  7. The labelled physical count count * (m+2)! * n! * n! is always even and is
     never equal to the count of a solvable puzzle.
  8. #SAT <-> #Jigsaw parsimonious translation on DIMACS-style CNFs.

Only the Python standard library is used.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
import math
import random
from typing import Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Lit = Tuple[int, int]
Clause = List[Lit]
Puzzle = List[Clause]
Cube = Tuple[int, ...]
SignedPerm = Tuple[Tuple[int, ...], Tuple[int, ...]]  # (perm, mask)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def fits(a: Cube, lit: Lit) -> bool:
    """A literal input mates with the variable piece at its socket."""
    return a[lit[0]] == lit[1]


def assembles(puzzle: Puzzle, a: Cube) -> bool:
    """Every clause piece has a mating input."""
    return all(any(fits(a, l) for l in c) for c in puzzle)


def cube(n: int) -> Iterable[Cube]:
    return itertools.product((0, 1), repeat=n)


def assemblies(puzzle: Puzzle, n: int) -> List[Cube]:
    return [a for a in cube(n) if assembles(puzzle, a)]


def count(puzzle: Puzzle, n: int) -> int:
    return len(assemblies(puzzle, n))


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hyperoctahedral action
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def act_lit(g: SignedPerm, lit: Lit) -> Lit:
    perm, mask = g
    i, p = lit
    return (perm[i], (p + mask[i]) % 2)


def act_puzzle(g: SignedPerm, puzzle: Puzzle) -> Puzzle:
    return [[act_lit(g, l) for l in c] for c in puzzle]


def act_cube(g: SignedPerm, a: Cube) -> Cube:
    perm, mask = g
    n = len(perm)
    inv = [0] * n
    for i, j in enumerate(perm):
        inv[j] = i
    return tuple((a[inv[j]] + mask[inv[j]]) % 2 for j in range(n))


def mul(g: SignedPerm, h: SignedPerm) -> SignedPerm:
    """g * h acts as 'first h, then g'."""
    gp, gm = g
    hp, hm = h
    n = len(gp)
    perm = tuple(gp[hp[i]] for i in range(n))
    mask = tuple((hm[i] + gm[hp[i]]) % 2 for i in range(n))
    return (perm, mask)


def complement(puzzle: Puzzle, n: int) -> Puzzle:
    """Global tab/blank swap: the signed permutation (id, all-ones)."""
    return act_puzzle((tuple(range(n)), (1,) * n), puzzle)


def all_signed_perms(n: int) -> List[SignedPerm]:
    return [(p, m) for p in itertools.permutations(range(n)) for m in cube(n)]


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mask symmetries and 2-adic divisibility
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def mask_symm(puzzle: Puzzle, n: int) -> List[Cube]:
    """Polarity masks mu whose flip maps the assembly space of P onto itself."""
    A = set(assemblies(puzzle, n))
    out = []
    for mu in cube(n):
        if {tuple((x + y) % 2 for x, y in zip(a, mu)) for a in A} == A:
            out.append(mu)
    return out


def v2(x: int) -> int:
    if x == 0:
        return 10 ** 9
    k = 0
    while x % 2 == 0:
        x //= 2
        k += 1
    return k


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mod-2 inclusion-exclusion and the affine-subcube criterion
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def falsifiers(clauses: Sequence[Clause], n: int) -> int:
    """Number of a falsifying every clause in the given subset."""
    return sum(1 for a in cube(n) if all(not any(fits(a, l) for l in c) for c in clauses))


def mod2_by_inclusion_exclusion(puzzle: Puzzle, n: int) -> int:
    total = 0
    for r in range(len(puzzle) + 1):
        for S in itertools.combinations(puzzle, r):
            total += falsifiers(S, n)
    return total % 2


def pins_consistently_everything(clauses: Sequence[Clause], n: int) -> bool:
    """Falsifying all of S forces a[i] = p+1 for each input (i,p); consistent & full?"""
    pinned: dict[int, int] = {}
    for c in clauses:
        for i, p in c:
            v = (p + 1) % 2
            if pinned.get(i, v) != v:
                return False
            pinned[i] = v
    return len(pinned) == n


def mod2_by_affine_criterion(puzzle: Puzzle, n: int) -> int:
    k = 0
    for r in range(len(puzzle) + 1):
        for S in itertools.combinations(puzzle, r):
            k += pins_consistently_everything(S, n)
    return k % 2


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Encoding: labelled physical assemblies
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def labelled_count(puzzle: Puzzle, n: int) -> int:
    m = len(puzzle)
    return count(puzzle, n) * math.factorial(m + 2) * math.factorial(n) ** 2


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SAT <-> Jigsaw
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def dimacs_to_puzzle(cnf: List[List[int]]) -> Puzzle:
    """DIMACS literal +v / -v (v >= 1) -> input at socket v-1, polarity 1 / 0."""
    return [[(abs(x) - 1, 1 if x > 0 else 0) for x in c] for c in cnf]


def puzzle_to_dimacs(puzzle: Puzzle) -> List[List[int]]:
    return [[(i + 1) if p == 1 else -(i + 1) for i, p in c] for c in puzzle]


def sat_count(cnf: List[List[int]], n: int) -> int:
    return sum(1 for a in cube(n)
               if all(any((a[abs(x) - 1] == 1) == (x > 0) for x in c) for c in cnf))


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def random_puzzle(n: int, m: int, width: int, rng: random.Random) -> Puzzle:
    return [[(rng.randrange(n), rng.randrange(2)) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, width))]
            for _ in range(m)]


def main() -> None:
    rng = random.Random(2026)

    print("=" * 72)
    print("1. A worked example")
    n = 3
    P: Puzzle = [[(0, 1), (1, 1)], [(1, 0), (2, 1)]]
    Pc = complement(P, n)
    print("  P        =", P)
    print("  comp(P)  =", Pc)
    print("  assemblies(P)       =", assemblies(P, n))
    print("  assemblies(comp(P)) =", assemblies(Pc, n))
    print("  counts:", count(P, n), count(Pc, n))

    print("=" * 72)
    print("2. Hyperoctahedral invariance with explicit witness bijection")
    checked = 0
    for _ in range(300):
        n = rng.randint(1, 4)
        Q = random_puzzle(n, rng.randint(0, 5), 3, rng)
        for g in rng.sample(all_signed_perms(n), min(6, 2 ** n * math.factorial(n))):
            A = assemblies(Q, n)
            B = set(assemblies(act_puzzle(g, Q), n))
            image = {act_cube(g, a) for a in A}
            assert image == B and len(image) == len(A)
            checked += 1
    print(f"  {checked} (puzzle, signed permutation) pairs: g maps assemblies(P) onto assemblies(gP)")

    print("=" * 72)
    print("3. Group law: (g*h).P == g.(h.P)")
    for _ in range(300):
        n = rng.randint(1, 4)
        Q = random_puzzle(n, 4, 3, rng)
        G = all_signed_perms(n)
        g, h = rng.choice(G), rng.choice(G)
        assert act_puzzle(mul(g, h), Q) == act_puzzle(g, act_puzzle(h, Q))
    print("  verified on 300 random triples")

    print("=" * 72)
    print("4. Complementation: parsimonious, involutive, size preserving, free")
    for n in range(1, 4):
        lits = [(i, p) for i in range(n) for p in (0, 1)]
        clauses = [list(c) for r in range(0, 3) for c in itertools.combinations(lits, r)]
        tot = 0
        for Q in itertools.product(clauses, repeat=2):
            Q = list(map(list, Q))
            Qc = complement(Q, n)
            assert count(Q, n) == count(Qc, n)
            for k in (2, 3, 5):
                assert count(Q, n) % k == count(Qc, n) % k
            assert complement(Qc, n) == Q
            assert sum(map(len, Q)) == sum(map(len, Qc))
            assert (Qc == Q) == all(len(c) == 0 for c in Q)
            tot += 1
        print(f"  n={n}: all {tot} two-clause puzzles (clause width <= 2) pass")

    print("=" * 72)
    print("5. 2-adic certificates from polarity-mask symmetries")
    stats = {"equal": 0, "gap": 0}
    for _ in range(400):
        n = rng.randint(1, 4)
        Q = random_puzzle(n, rng.randint(0, 4), 3, rng)
        c = count(Q, n)
        H = mask_symm(Q, n)
        k = int(math.log2(len(H)))
        assert 2 ** k == len(H) and c % len(H) == 0
        if c % 2 == 1:
            assert len(H) == 1
        g = rng.choice(all_signed_perms(n))
        assert len(mask_symm(act_puzzle(g, Q), n)) == len(H)
        if c > 0:
            stats["equal" if v2(c) == k else "gap"] += 1
    print("  |H| = 2^k divides count, odd count => H trivial, |H| invariant: OK")
    print(f"  among solvable samples: v2(count) = k in {stats['equal']}, strict gap in {stats['gap']}")

    print("=" * 72)
    print("6. Mod-2 count: signless inclusion-exclusion and affine-subcube criterion")
    for _ in range(300):
        n = rng.randint(1, 4)
        Q = random_puzzle(n, rng.randint(0, 5), 3, rng)
        c2 = count(Q, n) % 2
        assert c2 == mod2_by_inclusion_exclusion(Q, n) == mod2_by_affine_criterion(Q, n)
    print("  three ways of computing count mod 2 agree on 300 random puzzles")

    print("=" * 72)
    print("7. The encoding breaks parsimony")
    for n, Q in [(3, P), (2, [[(0, 1)], [(1, 0)]]), (2, [[(0, 1)], [(0, 0)]])]:
        c, L = count(Q, n), labelled_count(Q, n)
        print(f"  n={n}, m={len(Q)}: count={c:3d}  labelled={L:8d}  even={L % 2 == 0}"
              f"  parsimonious={L == c}")

    print("=" * 72)
    print("8. #SAT <-> #Jigsaw")
    for _ in range(200):
        n = rng.randint(1, 5)
        cnf = [[rng.choice([1, -1]) * rng.randint(1, n) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3))]
               for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 6))]
        Q = dimacs_to_puzzle(cnf)
        assert count(Q, n) == sat_count(cnf, n)
        assert puzzle_to_dimacs(Q) == cnf
    print("  translations are mutually inverse and count-preserving on 200 random CNFs")
    print("=" * 72)
    print("All checks passed.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Computational Evidence — Parsimonious complementation for jigsaw assembly counting

All numbers below are kernel-checked by `decide +kernel` in
`Catalog/Algebra/JigsawParsimony/Experiments.lean` unless marked *(exploratory)*;
exploratory figures come from `#eval` runs on the same definitions and are **not** formally verified.

## Instance family

`puzzlesN n` = all framed puzzles on `n` sockets with exactly two clause pieces, each
clause piece a sublist of the `2n` literal inputs.  `|puzzlesN 2| = 256`,
`|puzzlesN 3| = 4096`.

## 1. Complementation preserves the exact count (counterexample hunt)

| n | puzzles | `count (compPuzzle P) = count P` for all | status |
|---|---------|-------------------------------------------|--------|
| 2 | 256     | yes                                       | kernel-checked (`puzzlesN_two_comp_count`) |
| 3 | 4096    | yes                                       | kernel-checked (`puzzlesN_three_comp_count`) |

No counterexample found — consistent with the general theorem `count_compPuzzle`.

## 2. Count histograms

n = 2 (kernel-checked, `puzzlesN_two_histogram`):

| count | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|-------|---|---|---|---|---|
| #puzzles | 35 | 24 | 88 | 60 | 49 |

Odd count: 84 / 256.

n = 3 *(exploratory)*:

| count | 0 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 |
