\section{Introduction}

Reductions between combinatorial problems usually preserve only
\emph{solvability}. A reduction $f$ from a decision problem $A$ to a decision
problem $B$ only needs $x\in A\iff f(x)\in B$. Counting complexity asks for more.
A reduction is \emph{parsimonious} when the number of witnesses of $f(x)$ equals
the number of witnesses of $x$. Parsimonious reductions are the natural morphisms
of the class $\#\mathrm{P}$ introduced by Valiant. Since a parsimonious reduction
preserves the exact count, it also preserves the count modulo every $k$. So it
transports hardness for every modular counting class $\mathrm{Mod}_k\mathrm{P}$
at once, including $\oplus\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{Mod}_2\mathrm{P}$.

Jigsaw puzzles are a classical source of NP-complete problems. This paper studies
a framed variant in which the frame contributes $n$ binary \emph{variable sockets}
and the remaining pieces act as \emph{clauses}. The variant is designed so that
solving it is exactly satisfiability. The question we address is how the natural
symmetries of the instance space interact with counting. The most natural
symmetry is global complementation: swap every tab for a blank and vice versa.
This map is a bijection on instances, and we ask whether it is also a bijection
on \emph{witnesses}. If it is, it is a parsimonious self-reduction, and every
modular count is a complementation invariant.

We show that this is the case, and more. Complementation is one element of a
parsimonious action of the full hyperoctahedral group. The action has three
consequences:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Invariance.} The exact count is constant on orbits
  (Theorems~\ref{thm:bij} and~\ref{thm:action}), and hence so is every modular
  count (Corollary~\ref{cor:comp}).
\item \textbf{Freeness.} Complementation fixes no instance except the degenerate
  ones (Theorem~\ref{thm:free}).
\item \textbf{Divisibility.} Stabilisers in the translation subgroup produce
  powers of two dividing the count (Theorem~\ref{thm:2adic}).
\end{enumerate}
We also describe exactly where parsimony fails: in the physical encoding by
labelled pieces (Theorem~\ref{thm:enc}), not in the mathematics.

\emph{Scope.} The model of efficiency used here is the encoding-size bound: every
reduction we construct produces an output whose size is at most linear in the
input size. All of these maps are evidently computable in linear time. We do not
reprove that $\#$SAT is $\#$P-complete. We use the classical fact as a black box
and prove the parsimonious transfer from $\#$SAT to jigsaw counting.

\section{The model}

Throughout, $\F=\mathbb{Z}/2$ and $[n]=\{1,\dots,n\}$. We write the Boolean cube
additively: $Q_n=\F^{\,n}$. A coordinate $a_i=1$ means socket $i$ holds the tab
piece, and $a_i=0$ means it holds the blank.

\begin{definition}[Literal input, clause piece, framed puzzle]
A \emph{literal input} on $n$ sockets is a pair $\ell=(i,p)\in[n]\times\F$: a
socket together with the polarity it is milled for. A \emph{clause piece} is a
finite list of literal inputs. A \emph{framed puzzle} $P$ on $n$ sockets is a
finite list $P=(c_1,\dots,c_m)$ of clause pieces. Its \emph{size} is
$|P|=m+\sum_j|c_j|$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Fitting, assembling]
A literal input $(i,p)$ \emph{fits} a filling $a\in Q_n$ when $a_i=p$. A filling
$a$ \emph{assembles} $P$, written $a\models P$, when every clause piece contains a
literal input that fits:
\[
a\models P\quad:\Longleftrightarrow\quad\forall c\in P\ \exists(i,p)\in c:\ a_i=p .
\]
The \emph{assembly space} is $\A(P)=\{a\in Q_n: a\models P\}$, and the
\emph{assembly count} is $\#P=|\A(P)|$.
\end{definition}

A literal $(i,1)$ is the positive literal $x_i$ and $(i,0)$ is the negative
literal $\lnot x_i$. Under this dictionary a puzzle is a CNF formula,
$a\models P$ is satisfaction, and $\#P$ is the number of satisfying assignments.
A clause piece with no inputs can never snap in, so a puzzle containing one has
$\#P=0$. The empty puzzle has $\#P=2^n$.

\begin{example}\label{ex:main}
Let $n=3$ and $P=\big((1,1),(2,1)\big),\big((2,0),(3,1)\big)$, i.e.\
$(x_1\lor x_2)\land(\lnot x_2\lor x_3)$. Then
$\A(P)=\{011,100,101,111\}$ (written $a_1a_2a_3$) and $\#P=4$.
\end{example}

\section{The hyperoctahedral action}

\begin{definition}[Signed permutation]
A \emph{signed permutation} is a pair $g=(\sigma,\mu)$ with $\sigma\in S_n$ and
$\mu\in Q_n$. It acts on literal inputs, puzzles and fillings by
\[
g\cdot(i,p)=(\sigma(i),\,p+\mu_i),\qquad
g\cdot P=\big((g\cdot\ell)_{\ell\in c}\big)_{c\in P},\qquad
(g\cdot a)_j=a_{\sigma^{-1}(j)}+\mu_{\sigma^{-1}(j)} .
\]
That is, socket $i$ is relabelled $\sigma(i)$, and the polarity at socket $i$ is
flipped exactly when $\mu_i=1$. The inverse action on fillings is
$(g^{-1}\cdot b)_i=b_{\sigma(i)}-\mu_i$. It satisfies
$g^{-1}\cdot(g\cdot a)=a$ and $g\cdot(g^{-1}\cdot b)=b$, so $a\mapsto g\cdot a$ is
a bijection of $Q_n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Literal-level transport]\label{lem:lit}
For all $g$, $a$ and $\ell$: $g\cdot\ell$ fits $g\cdot a$ if and only if $\ell$
fits $a$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Let $\ell=(i,p)$. Then $(g\cdot a)_{\sigma(i)}=a_i+\mu_i$ and
$g\cdot\ell=(\sigma(i),p+\mu_i)$. So the condition reads $a_i+\mu_i=p+\mu_i$,
which is equivalent to $a_i=p$ by cancellation in $\F$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Witness-preserving bijection]\label{thm:bij}
For every signed permutation $g$, every puzzle $P$ and every filling $a$,
$g\cdot a\models g\cdot P\iff a\models P$. Consequently $a\mapsto g\cdot a$
restricts to a bijection $\A(P)\to\A(g\cdot P)$ with inverse
$b\mapsto g^{-1}\cdot b$. Equivalently $\A(g\cdot P)=g\cdot\A(P)$, and in
particular $\#(g\cdot P)=\#P$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The clause pieces of $g\cdot P$ are the images $g\cdot c$ of the clause pieces
$c$ of $P$, and the inputs of $g\cdot c$ are the images of the inputs of $c$.
Suppose $a\models P$, and take a clause piece $g\cdot c$. Choose an input
$\ell\in c$ that fits $a$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:lit}, $g\cdot\ell$ fits $g\cdot a$.
Conversely, suppose $g\cdot a\models g\cdot P$ and take $c\in P$. Some input of
$g\cdot c$ fits $g\cdot a$. That input has the form $g\cdot\ell$ with $\ell\in c$,
and Lemma~\ref{lem:lit} shows $\ell$ fits $a$. The two maps on fillings are
mutually inverse, so the restriction is a bijection.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Group law]
Define $gh=(\sigma_g\sigma_h,\nu)$ with $\nu_i=\mu_{h,i}+\mu_{g,\sigma_h(i)}$. The
product means ``first $h$, then $g$''. This is the multiplication of the wreath
product $\F\wr S_n=B_n$, a group of order $2^n n!$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Action compatibility and orbit invariance]\label{thm:action}
For all $g,h$ and $P$, $(gh)\cdot P=g\cdot(h\cdot P)$. Consequently, for any
finite word $g_1\cdots g_r$ of signed permutations,
$\#\big(g_1\cdot(g_2\cdot(\cdots(g_r\cdot P)\cdots))\big)=\#P$, so the assembly
count is constant on every $B_n$-orbit.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
On literal inputs,
$g\cdot(h\cdot(i,p))=(\sigma_g\sigma_h(i),\,p+\mu_{h,i}+\mu_{g,\sigma_h(i)})=(gh)\cdot(i,p)$.
Mapping over clause pieces and over the puzzle preserves this identity. Orbit
invariance follows by induction on the length of the word, using
Theorem~\ref{thm:bij} at each step.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
$B_n$ is the symmetry group of the $n$-cube, and $a\mapsto g\cdot a$ is the
corresponding Hamming isometry of $Q_n$. Theorem~\ref{thm:bij} says that
transforming the instance moves the solution set by a cube symmetry. Every
invariant of subsets of $Q_n$ under cube symmetries is therefore an invariant of
puzzles.
\end{remark}

\section{Complementation as a parsimonious self-reduction}

\begin{definition}[Complement]
The \emph{complement} of $P$ is $\comp P=(\mathrm{id},\mathbf 1)\cdot P$,
obtained by replacing every input $(i,p)$ with $(i,p+1)$. On fillings,
$(\mathrm{id},\mathbf 1)$ acts by bitwise negation $a\mapsto a+\mathbf 1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Complementation is parsimonious]\label{cor:comp}
For every puzzle $P$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $a\models P\iff a+\mathbf 1\models\comp P$, so bitwise negation is an
  explicit bijection $\A(P)\to\A(\comp P)$;
\item $\#\comp P=\#P$;
\item $\#\comp P\equiv\#P\pmod k$ for every $k\ge1$; in particular $\#P$ is even
  if and only if $\#\comp P$ is even;
\item $\comp{\comp P}=P$ and $|\comp P|=|P|$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Items (1)--(3) are Theorem~\ref{thm:bij} with $g=(\mathrm{id},\mathbf 1)$. Item
(4) holds because $p+1+1=p$ in $\F$ and the shape is unchanged.
\end{proof}

A \emph{counting problem} is a set of instances $X$ with a size function and a
count $c_X:X\to\mathbb N$. A \emph{parsimonious reduction} from $(X,c_X)$ to
$(Y,c_Y)$ is a map $f:X\to Y$ with $c_Y(f(x))=c_X(x)$ and $|f(x)|\le C|x|+D$ for
constants $C,D$. Corollary~\ref{cor:comp} shows that complementation is a
parsimonious self-reduction of $\#\mathrm{Jigsaw}$ with $C=1$, $D=0$. It is
computable in a single linear pass.

\begin{theorem}[Freeness]\label{thm:free}
$\comp P=P$ if and only if every clause piece of $P$ is empty.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
If all clause pieces are empty there is nothing to flip. Conversely, $\comp P$
has the same shape as $P$. If some clause piece has an input $(i,p)$, the
corresponding position of $\comp P$ holds $(i,p+1)\neq(i,p)$.
\end{proof}

Thus complementation acts freely on the non-degenerate puzzles. That part of the
instance space is partitioned into pairs $\{P,\comp P\}$ of distinct instances
with equal counts.

\section{Mask symmetries and \texorpdfstring{$2$}{2}-adic certificates}

\begin{definition}[Mask-symmetry group]
For a puzzle $P$ let $H_P=\{\mu\in Q_n:\A(P)+\mu=\A(P)\}$, the stabiliser of the
assembly space under translations. It is an $\F$-linear subspace of $Q_n$. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:bij}, every mask $\mu$ with $(\mathrm{id},\mu)\cdot P=P$ lies in
$H_P$, so the results below apply to those masks as well.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[$2$-adic certificate]\label{thm:2adic}
For every puzzle $P$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $|H_P|=2^k$ with $k=\dim H_P$, and $\#P=2^k\cdot|\A(P)/H_P|$; in
  particular $2^k\mid\#P$;
\item $|H_{g\cdot P}|=|H_P|$ for every signed permutation $g$;
\item if $\#P$ is odd then $H_P=\{0\}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
(1) $H_P$ acts freely on $\A(P)$ by translation, because $a+\mu=a$ forces
$\mu=0$. All orbits therefore have size $|H_P|$. (2) For $g=(\sigma,\mu_g)$ one
computes $g\cdot(a+\nu)=g\cdot a+\nu\circ\sigma^{-1}$. Together with
$\A(g\cdot P)=g\cdot\A(P)$ this gives
$H_{g\cdot P}=\{\nu\circ\sigma^{-1}:\nu\in H_P\}$. (3) If $2^k$ divides an odd
number then $k=0$.
\end{proof}

Let $v_2$ denote the $2$-adic valuation. The certificate is often sharp: on
random puzzles with $n\le4$, $v_2(\#P)=k$ held in $242$ of $243$ solvable samples.
By (1), the gap $v_2(\#P)-k$ equals $v_2$ of the number of $H_P$-orbits on
$\A(P)$.

\section{The parity of the count}

\begin{theorem}[Mod-$2$ count by signless inclusion--exclusion]\label{thm:ie}
For a set $S$ of clause pieces let $F_S$ be the set of fillings at which every
$c\in S$ fails. Then $\#P\equiv\sum_{S\subseteq P}|F_S|\pmod 2$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Inclusion--exclusion gives $\#P=\sum_S(-1)^{|S|}|F_S|$, and $-1\equiv1\pmod2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Affine-subcube criterion]\label{prop:affine}
Each $F_S$ is empty or an affine subcube. Call $S$ \emph{consistent} if no socket
is forced to both values, and \emph{fully pinning} if every socket occurs in an
input of some clause of $S$. Then
\[
\#P\equiv\big|\{S\subseteq P: S\text{ consistent and fully pinning}\}\big|\pmod2 .
\]
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
A clause piece $c$ fails at $a$ exactly when $a_i=p+1$ for every
$(i,p)\in c$. So $F_S$ is cut out by pinning constraints. It is empty on
conflict, and otherwise has $2^{\,n-|V(S)|}$ elements, where $V(S)$ is the set of
pinned sockets. That number is odd exactly when $V(S)=[n]$. Apply
Theorem~\ref{thm:ie}.
\end{proof}

In Example~\ref{ex:main}, $|F_\varnothing|=8$, $|F_{\{c_1\}}|=|F_{\{c_2\}}|=2$
and $|F_{\{c_1,c_2\}}|=0$. No subset is fully pinning, and indeed
$\#P=8-2-2+0=4$ is even.

\section{Encodings: where parsimony breaks}

\subsection{SAT and jigsaw reduce to each other parsimoniously}
A DIMACS CNF on variables $1,\dots,n$ translates to a puzzle by
$+v\mapsto(v,1)$ and $-v\mapsto(v,0)$, preserving shape.

\begin{theorem}[Two-way parsimony]\label{thm:sat}
The translations $\mathrm{CNF}\to\mathrm{Puzzle}$ and
$\mathrm{Puzzle}\to\mathrm{CNF}$ are mutually inverse, size-preserving and
parsimonious.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[Hardness transfer]
If a counting problem reduces parsimoniously to $\#$SAT, then it reduces
parsimoniously to $\#$Jigsaw, and hence, for every $k$, to computing
$\#P\bmod k$. Since $\#$SAT is $\#$P-complete under parsimonious reductions,
exact jigsaw assembly counting is $\#$P-complete, and computing $\#P\bmod k$ is
$\mathrm{Mod}_k\mathrm{P}$-hard.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Parsimonious maps with linear size bounds compose to such maps.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Labelled physical assemblies}
To build a physical jigsaw, a framed puzzle with $m$ clause pieces on $n$
sockets is encoded as a pile of labelled pieces. Some of those pieces are
physically interchangeable; the multiplicity factor below records the
relabellings of interchangeable pieces (one family of size $m+2$ and two families
of size $n$).

\begin{theorem}[The encoding breaks parsimony]\label{thm:enc}
The number of labelled physical assemblies is
$\#_{\mathrm{lab}}(P)=\#P\cdot(m+2)!\cdot n!\cdot n!$. Consequently
$\#_{\mathrm{lab}}(P)$ is always even, $\#_{\mathrm{lab}}(P)=0\iff\#P=0$, and if
$\#P>0$ then $\#_{\mathrm{lab}}(P)\neq\#P$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Each mathematical assembly lifts to exactly $(m+2)!(n!)^2$ labelled ones. Since
$(m+2)!\ge2$, the product is even and strictly exceeds $\#P$ when $\#P\ge1$.
\end{proof}

The symmetry $P\mapsto\comp P$ preserves all counting information. The physical
encoding keeps only the zero/nonzero distinction. Indeed, the factor
$(m+2)!(n!)^2$ is divisible by every prime $q\le m+2$, so the encoding erases
every $\mathrm{Mod}_q$ count for such $q$. Piece multiplicities carry counting
information.

\section{Algorithms and experiments}

\textbf{Brute-force count:} enumerate $Q_n$, cost $O(2^n|P|)$.
\textbf{Witness transport:} $a\mapsto g\cdot a$ in $O(n)$ time, landing in
$\A(g\cdot P)$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:bij}.
\textbf{Parity by pinning:} for each $S\subseteq P$ propagate forced values,
abort on conflict, count fully pinning subsets; cost $O(2^m|P|)$, preferable when
$m<n$.
\textbf{Mask-symmetry group:} test $\A(P)+\mu=\A(P)$ for each $\mu$; cost
$O(2^n\#P)$.

We tested the results above on enumerated and random instances.
Theorem~\ref{thm:bij} was checked on $1440$ random (puzzle, signed permutation)
pairs, and Theorem~\ref{thm:action} on $300$ random triples.
Corollary~\ref{cor:comp} and Theorem~\ref{thm:free} were checked exhaustively on
all two-clause puzzles of clause width at most $2$ for $n=1,2,3$ ($16$, $121$
and $484$ puzzles). Theorem~\ref{thm:2adic} was checked on $400$ random puzzles,
Theorem~\ref{thm:ie} and Proposition~\ref{prop:affine} on $300$, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:sat} on $200$ random CNFs. For Example~\ref{ex:main},
$\#_{\mathrm{lab}}=4\cdot4!\cdot3!\cdot3!=3456$ while $\#P=4$.

\section{Discussion and future work}

Complementation was conjectured to be a parsimonious self-reduction, making the
mod-$2$ count a complementation invariant while the exact count stays
$\#$P-hard. This holds because the hyperoctahedral group acts compatibly on
instances and witnesses. The symmetry gives no shortcut to the count. It does
give free equivalences between instances, useful for canonicalisation and
symmetry breaking, and $2$-adic arithmetic information through stabilisers.

Open directions:
(1) a Burnside census of $B_n$-orbits of two-clause puzzles over signed cycle
types;
(2) characterising when $v_2(\#P)=\log_2|H_P|$, i.e.\ when the number of
$H_P$-orbits on $\A(P)$ is odd;
(3) parity-tractable families detected by Proposition~\ref{prop:affine};
(4) physical encodings with odd, or trivial, multiplicity factor.

"""
Parity-Preserving Self-Reduction for Jigsaw Assembly Counting -- numerical demo.

A framed jigsaw puzzle on n sockets is a list of clause pieces; each clause piece is
a list of literal inputs (i, p) with i a socket in {0,...,n-1} and p a polarity in
{0,1} (0 = blank, 1 = tab).  A choice a in {0,1}^n of variable pieces *assembles*
the puzzle when every clause piece has an input (i, p) with a[i] == p.

This script checks, on exhaustively enumerated and random small instances:

  1. Signed-permutation (hyperoctahedral) invariance of the assembly count, via an
     explicit witness bijection.
  2. Compatibility of the action with the group law of signed permutations.
  3. Global complementation is a parsimonious, involutive, size-preserving
     self-reduction; every modular count is a complementation invariant.
  4. Complementation is free away from puzzles whose clause pieces are all empty.
  5. 2-adic divisibility: the polarity-mask symmetry group has order 2^k dividing
     the count; odd counts force a trivial symmetry group; the order is a
     hyperoctahedral invariant.
  6. The mod-2 count via signless inclusion-exclusion, and the affine-subcube
     criterion (only consistent, fully pinning clause subsets contribute).
  7. The labelled physical count count * (m+2)! * n! * n! is always even and is
     never equal to the count of a solvable puzzle.
  8. #SAT <-> #Jigsaw parsimonious translation on DIMACS-style CNFs.

Only the Python standard library is used.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
import math
import random
from typing import Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Lit = Tuple[int, int]
Clause = List[Lit]
Puzzle = List[Clause]
Cube = Tuple[int, ...]
SignedPerm = Tuple[Tuple[int, ...], Tuple[int, ...]]  # (perm, mask)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def fits(a: Cube, lit: Lit) -> bool:
    """A literal input mates with the variable piece at its socket."""
    return a[lit[0]] == lit[1]


def assembles(puzzle: Puzzle, a: Cube) -> bool:
    """Every clause piece has a mating input."""
    return all(any(fits(a, l) for l in c) for c in puzzle)


def cube(n: int) -> Iterable[Cube]:
    return itertools.product((0, 1), repeat=n)


def assemblies(puzzle: Puzzle, n: int) -> List[Cube]:
    return [a for a in cube(n) if assembles(puzzle, a)]


def count(puzzle: Puzzle, n: int) -> int:
    return len(assemblies(puzzle, n))


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hyperoctahedral action
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def act_lit(g: SignedPerm, lit: Lit) -> Lit:
    perm, mask = g
    i, p = lit
    return (perm[i], (p + mask[i]) % 2)


def act_puzzle(g: SignedPerm, puzzle: Puzzle) -> Puzzle:
    return [[act_lit(g, l) for l in c] for c in puzzle]


def act_cube(g: SignedPerm, a: Cube) -> Cube:
    perm, mask = g
    n = len(perm)
    inv = [0] * n
    for i, j in enumerate(perm):
        inv[j] = i
    return tuple((a[inv[j]] + mask[inv[j]]) % 2 for j in range(n))


def mul(g: SignedPerm, h: SignedPerm) -> SignedPerm:
    """g * h acts as 'first h, then g'."""
    gp, gm = g
    hp, hm = h
    n = len(gp)
    perm = tuple(gp[hp[i]] for i in range(n))
    mask = tuple((hm[i] + gm[hp[i]]) % 2 for i in range(n))
    return (perm, mask)


def complement(puzzle: Puzzle, n: int) -> Puzzle:
    """Global tab/blank swap: the signed permutation (id, all-ones)."""
    return act_puzzle((tuple(range(n)), (1,) * n), puzzle)


def all_signed_perms(n: int) -> List[SignedPerm]:
    return [(p, m) for p in itertools.permutations(range(n)) for m in cube(n)]


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mask symmetries and 2-adic divisibility
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def mask_symm(puzzle: Puzzle, n: int) -> List[Cube]:
    """Polarity masks mu whose flip maps the assembly space of P onto itself."""
    A = set(assemblies(puzzle, n))
    out = []
    for mu in cube(n):
        if {tuple((x + y) % 2 for x, y in zip(a, mu)) for a in A} == A:
            out.append(mu)
    return out


def v2(x: int) -> int:
    if x == 0:
        return 10 ** 9
    k = 0
    while x % 2 == 0:
        x //= 2
        k += 1
    return k


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mod-2 inclusion-exclusion and the affine-subcube criterion
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def falsifiers(clauses: Sequence[Clause], n: int) -> int:
    """Number of a falsifying every clause in the given subset."""
    return sum(1 for a in cube(n) if all(not any(fits(a, l) for l in c) for c in clauses))


def mod2_by_inclusion_exclusion(puzzle: Puzzle, n: int) -> int:
    total = 0
    for r in range(len(puzzle) + 1):
        for S in itertools.combinations(puzzle, r):
            total += falsifiers(S, n)
    return total % 2


def pins_consistently_everything(clauses: Sequence[Clause], n: int) -> bool:
    """Falsifying all of S forces a[i] = p+1 for each input (i,p); consistent & full?"""
    pinned: dict[int, int] = {}
    for c in clauses:
        for i, p in c:
            v = (p + 1) % 2
            if pinned.get(i, v) != v:

*A guided tour of why swapping every tab for a blank never changes how many ways a jigsaw can be finished, and of where counting information really gets lost.*

## 1. A jigsaw that is secretly a logic formula

A **framed puzzle** has $n$ sockets. Each socket receives either a tab ($1$) or a blank ($0$), so a filling is a point $a\in\{0,1\}^n$, a corner of the $n$-dimensional cube. A **clause piece** carries connectors $(i,p)$: socket $i$, polarity $p$. It snaps in when at least one connector mates, i.e. $a_i = p$. The puzzle is **assembled** when every clause piece snaps in.

So a puzzle *is* a CNF formula, and assemblies are satisfying assignments. The **assembly count** $\#P$ is exactly the quantity computed by [#SAT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharp-SAT).

<details><summary>Background: decision, counting and parity classes</summary>

Deciding whether $\#P>0$ is SAT, which is [NP-complete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cook%E2%80%93Levin_theorem). Computing $\#P$ exactly is [#P-complete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E2%99%AFP-complete) (Valiant, 1979). Computing $\#P \bmod 2$ is complete for [⊕P](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parity_P). By [Toda's theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toda%27s_theorem) the whole polynomial hierarchy lies in $\mathrm{P}^{\#\mathrm{P}}$, and the proof runs through parity counting. A **parsimonious** reduction preserves the exact number of witnesses, and hence every modular count.
</details>

Try it yourself: the laboratory below starts with $(x_1\lor x_2)\land(\lnot x_2\lor x_3)$, which has four assemblies.

## 2. The flip

Press **Complement**. Every connector $(i,p)$ becomes $(i,1-p)$. The green corners move, but their number stays the same: each new assembly is the bitwise negation of an old one.

{{visualization:0}}

> **Complementation Theorem.** $a \models P \iff a+\mathbf 1 \models \overline P$. Hence $\#\overline P = \#P$, and $\#\overline P\equiv \#P \pmod k$ for every $k$. The map is linear-time, size-preserving and involutive: a **parsimonious self-reduction**.

## 3. A whole group of flips

The flip is one element of the **hyperoctahedral group** $B_n=(\mathbb Z/2)^n\rtimes S_n$ of signed permutations $g=(\sigma,\mu)$. Each one relabels socket $i$ as $\sigma(i)$ and flips the polarity where $\mu_i=1$. Use *Random signed permutation* in the laboratory and watch the "history of counts" row: it never changes.

<details><summary>Click to reveal the proof of hyperoctahedral invariance</summary>

Define $g\cdot(i,p) = (\sigma(i), p+\mu_i)$ and $(g\cdot a)_{\sigma(i)} = a_i+\mu_i$. Then $g\cdot(i,p)$ fits $g\cdot a$ iff $a_i+\mu_i = p+\mu_i$ iff $a_i=p$. Applying this connector by connector and clause by clause gives $g\cdot a\models g\cdot P \iff a\models P$. The map $a\mapsto g\cdot a$ is a bijection of the cube with inverse $(g^{-1}b)_i = b_{\sigma(i)}-\mu_i$, so it restricts to a bijection of assembly spaces. Compatibility with the group law, $(gh)\cdot P = g\cdot(h\cdot P)$, holds connector by connector because $\mu_{h,i}+\mu_{g,\sigma_h(i)}$ is the mask of $gh$.
</details>

The witness bijection is completely explicit:

{{algorithm:0}}

**Freeness.** $\overline P = P$ happens only when every clause piece is empty, because a single connector $(i,p)$ becomes $(i,1-p)$. Away from these degenerate puzzles, instances come in distinct pairs $\{P,\overline P\}$ with equal counts.

## 4. Symmetry forces powers of two

Let $H_P$ be the set of masks $\mu$ with $\mathcal A(P)+\mu = \mathcal A(P)$. It is a subgroup of $(\mathbb Z/2)^n$, so $|H_P| = 2^k$. It acts **freely** on the assemblies.

> **2-adic Certificate Theorem.** $2^k$ divides $\#P$; $|H_{g\cdot P}| = |H_P|$ for every signed permutation; an odd count forces $H_P$ to be trivial.

In the laboratory, try the puzzle `1 -1 | 2` with $n=3$. Socket 3 never matters, and neither does socket 1, so $H_P$ has order $4$ and $\#P=4$.

{{algorithm:2}}

How sharp is the certificate? Almost always exactly sharp:

{{visualization:1}}

<details><summary>Why the gap is the parity of the number of orbits</summary>
Since every $H_P$-orbit has exactly $2^k$ elements, $\#P = 2^k\cdot|\mathcal A(P)/H_P|$. Thus $v_2(\#P) - k = v_2(\#\text{orbits})$, and the certificate is sharp exactly when the number of orbits is odd.
</details>

## 5. Parity without counting

Inclusion–exclusion gives $\#P = \sum_S (-1)^{|S|}|F_S|$, where $F_S$ is the set of fillings at which every clause in $S$ fails. Modulo 2 the signs vanish. Each $F_S$ is empty or a subcube of size $2^{\,n-\#\text{pinned sockets}}$, which is odd only when every socket is pinned. Panel 5 of the laboratory lists every subset.

> **Affine-subcube criterion.** $\#P \equiv \#\{S : S \text{ consistent and pins all } n \text{ sockets}\} \pmod 2$.

{{algorithm:1}}

## 6. Where parsimony actually breaks

DIMACS formulas and puzzles translate into each other **parsimoniously**, so every hardness result for counting SAT solutions, exact or modular, transfers to jigsaws. The *physical* encoding behaves differently. Labelled pieces turn each assembly into $(m+2)!\,n!\,n!$ labelled assemblies:

$$\#_{\text{lab}}(P) = \#P\cdot(m+2)!\cdot n!\cdot n!.$$

This number is always even, and it differs from $\#P$ on every solvable puzzle. The encoding keeps solvability and erases the parity (watch the "labelled physical count" row in the laboratory). **Piece multiplicities carry counting information.** The mathematics preserves it and the packaging destroys it.

# A mod-2 inclusion–exclusion formula for the assembly count

Over `ZMod 2` the indicator that a clause piece fits is `1 + [the piece is
falsified]`, so expanding the product over clause pieces yields an inclusion–
exclusion formula with no signs:

`count P ≡ ∑_{S ⊆ clause pieces} #{a : a falsifies every piece in S}  (mod 2)`.

Combined with `count_compPuzzle`, the falsifier sums of `P` and of its complement
agree mod 2 (`falsifierSum_compPuzzle`).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace JigsawParsimony

open Finset

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- A choice of variable pieces *falsifies* a clause piece when none of its inputs
mates. -/
def Falsifies (a : Cube n) (c : ClausePiece n) : Prop := ∀ l ∈ c, ¬ Fits a l

instance (a : Cube n) (c : ClausePiece n) : Decidable (Falsifies a c) := by
  unfold Falsifies; infer_instance

/-- Number of choices of variable pieces falsifying every clause piece indexed by
`S`. -/
def falsifierCount (P : Puzzle n) (S : Finset (Fin P.length)) : ℕ :=
  (univ.filter fun a : Cube n => ∀ i ∈ S, Falsifies a (P.get i)).card

theorem assembles_iff_forall_get (P : Puzzle n) (a : Cube n) :
    Assembles P a ↔ ∀ i : Fin P.length, ¬ Falsifies a (P.get i) := by
  unfold Assembles Falsifies
  simp only [not_forall, not_not, exists_prop]
  constructor
  · intro h i
    exact h _ (List.get_mem P i)
  · intro h c hc
    obtain ⟨i, rfl⟩ := List.get_of_mem hc
    exact h i

theorem fits_indicator (p : Prop) [Decidable p] :
    ((if ¬ p then 1 else 0 : ZMod 2)) = 1 + (if p then 1 else 0) := by
  by_cases hp : p <;> simp [hp]
  decide

/-- **Signless inclusion–exclusion mod 2.** -/
theorem count_cast_zmod_two (P : Puzzle n) :
    (count P : ZMod 2) = ∑ S ∈ (univ : Finset (Fin P.length)).powerset,
      (falsifierCount P S : ZMod 2) := by
  have h1 : (count P : ZMod 2) =

    rw [count, assemblies, ← Finset.sum_boole]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
    rw [Finset.prod_boole]
    simp only [Finset.mem_univ, true_implies, assembles_iff_forall_get]
  rw [h1]
  simp_rw [fits_indicator, Finset.prod_one_add, Finset.prod_boole]
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun S _ => ?_
  rw [falsifierCount, Finset.natCast_card_filter]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
  congr 1

/-- The same formula as a congruence of natural numbers. -/
theorem count_modEq_falsifierSum (P : Puzzle n) :
    count P ≡ ∑ S ∈ (univ : Finset (Fin P.length)).powerset, falsifierCount P S [MOD 2] := by
  rw [← ZMod.natCast_eq_natCast_iff, count_cast_zmod_two, Nat.cast_sum]

  simp [compPuzzle]

/-!
# The encoding, not the mathematics, breaks parsimony

The abstract assembly count (`count`) counts *choices of variable pieces*.  A
physical jigsaw solver, however, places *labelled* physical pieces into slots, and
the piece-count encoding of the SAT reduction uses many physically identical
pieces: `2` corner pieces and `m` clause pieces of one boundary shape (here called
`frame`), `n` identical tab variable pieces and `n` identical blank variable pieces,
for `2n + m + 2` pieces in total.

A *labelled assembly* is an abstract assembly together with a shape-preserving
relabelling of the physical pieces.  We prove:

* `card_relabel_eq_prod` (general multiplicity law) : for an arbitrary shape map,
  the number of shape-preserving relabellings is `∏ (multiplicity)!`, and it is `1`
  exactly when the shape map is injective (`prod_factorial_eq_one_iff`).
* `card_labeledAssembly` : for the SAT encoding,
  `#labelled = count P · (m+2)! · n! · n!`.
* `even_card_labeledAssembly` : the labelled count is always even, so it carries no
  mod-2 information at all, whereas `count` can be odd (`labeled_parity_collapse`).
* `labeled_not_parsimonious` : labelled counting is parsimonious for *no* solvable
  puzzle — piece multiplicities, not complementation, are what break parsimony.
* `count_eq_card_labeled_div` : the exact count is recovered by dividing out the
  multiplicity factor, so the multiplicities carry exactly the lost counting data.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace JigsawParsimony

open Finset

/-! ## General multiplicity law -/

theorem card_subtype_sum {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] (p : α ⊕ β → Prop)
    [DecidablePred p] :
    Fintype.card {x // p x} =
      Fintype.card {a // p (Sum.inl a)} + Fintype.card {b // p (Sum.inr b)} := by
  rw [← Fintype.card_sum]
  exact Fintype.card_congr Equiv.subtypeSum

/-- Number of shape-preserving relabellings of a finite set of pieces. -/
theorem card_relabel_eq_prod {α ι : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq ι]
    [Fintype ι] (f : α → ι) :
    Fintype.card {g : Equiv.Perm α // f ∘ g = f} = ∏ i, (Fintype.card {a // f a = i}).factorial :=
  DomMulAct.stabilizer_card f

/-- The multiplicity factor is trivial exactly when no two pieces share a shape. -/
theorem prod_factorial_eq_one_iff {α ι : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι]
    (f : α → ι) :
    ∏ i, (Fintype.card {a // f a = i}).factorial = 1 ↔ Function.Injective f := by
  rw [Finset.prod_eq_one_iff_of_one_le'
    (fun i _ => Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.2 (Nat.factorial_ne_zero _))]
  simp only [Finset.mem_univ, true_implies, Nat.factorial_eq_one]
  constructor
  · intro h x y hxy
    exact congrArg Subtype.val (Fintype.card_le_one_iff.1 (h (f y)) ⟨x, hxy⟩ ⟨y, rfl⟩)
  · intro hf i
    exact Fintype.card_le_one_iff.2 fun a b => Subtype.ext (hf (a.2.trans b.2.symm))

/-! ## The physical pieces of the SAT encoding -/

/-- Physical piece shapes used by the encoding. -/
inductive PieceShape
  | frame
  | tabVar
  | blankVar
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- Physical slots: `m + 2` frame-shaped pieces (two corners and `m` clause pieces),
`n` tab variable pieces, and `n` blank variable pieces. -/
abbrev Slot (n m : ℕ) := Fin (m + 2) ⊕ Fin n ⊕ Fin n

/-- The shape of the physical piece in each slot. -/
def slotShape {n m : ℕ} : Slot n m → PieceShape :=
  Sum.elim (fun _ => .frame) (Sum.elim (fun _ => .tabVar) (fun _ => .blankVar))

/-- The encoding uses exactly `2n + m + 2` physical pieces. -/
theorem card_slot (n m : ℕ) : Fintype.card (Slot n m) = 2 * n + m + 2 := by
  simp only [Fintype.card_sum, Fintype.card_fin]; ring

theorem card_frame (n m : ℕ) :
    Fintype.card {a : Slot n m // slotShape a = .frame} = m + 2 := by
  rw [card_subtype_sum, card_subtype_sum]; simp [slotShape]

theorem card_tabVar (n m : ℕ) :
    Fintype.card {a : Slot n m // slotShape a = .tabVar} = n := by
  rw [card_subtype_sum, card_subtype_sum]; simp [slotShape]

theorem card_blankVar (n m : ℕ) :
    Fintype.card {a : Slot n m // slotShape a = .blankVar} = n := by
  rw [card_subtype_sum, card_subtype_sum]; simp [slotShape]

/-- Shape-preserving relabellings of the physical pieces. -/
abbrev Relabel (n m : ℕ) := {g : Equiv.Perm (Slot n m) // slotShape ∘ g = slotShape}

/-- **Multiplicity factor of the encoding.** -/
theorem card_relabel (n m : ℕ) :
    Fintype.card (Relabel n m) = (m + 2).factorial * n.factorial * n.factorial := by
  rw [card_relabel_eq_prod, Fintype.prod_eq_mul_prod_compl PieceShape.frame]
  have hcompl : ({PieceShape.frame}ᶜ : Finset PieceShape) = {.tabVar, .blankVar} := by decide
  rw [hcompl, Finset.prod_pair (by decide), card_frame, card_tabVar, card_blankVar, mul_assoc]

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- A labelled assembly: an abstract assembly together with a shape-preserving
relabelling of the `2n + m + 2` physical pieces. -/
abbrev LabeledAssembly (P : Puzzle n) := {a : Cube n // Assembles P a} × Relabel n P.length

/-- **Labelled count = abstract count × multiplicity factor.** -/
theorem card_labeledAssembly (P : Puzzle n) :
    Fintype.card (LabeledAssembly P) =
      count P * ((P.length + 2).factorial * n.factorial * n.factorial) := by
  rw [Fintype.card_prod, card_relabel, ← count_eq_card_subtype]

theorem even_card_labeledAssembly (P : Puzzle n) : Even (Fintype.card (LabeledAssembly P)) := by
  rw [card_labeledAssembly]
  have h2 : 2 ∣ (P.length + 2).factorial := Nat.dvd_factorial (by norm_num) (by omega)
  exact even_iff_two_dvd.2 (Dvd.dvd.mul_left (Dvd.dvd.mul_right (Dvd.dvd.mul_right h2 _) _) _)

theorem labeled_not_parsimonious (P : Puzzle n) (hP : 0 < count P) :
    Fintype.card (LabeledAssembly P) ≠ count P := by
  rw [card_labeledAssembly]
  intro h
  have hf : (P.length + 2).factorial * n.factorial * n.factorial = 1 := by
    have := Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_left hP (h.trans (mul_one _).symm)
    exact this
  have h2 : 2 ≤ (P.length + 2).factorial := by
    calc 2 = (2 : ℕ).factorial := rfl
      _ ≤ (P.length + 2).factorial := Nat.factorial_le (by omega)
  have : (P.length + 2).factorial ≤ 1 := by
    rw [← hf, mul_assoc]
    exact Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (Nat.mul_pos (Nat.factorial_pos _) (Nat.factorial_pos _))
  omega

theorem count_eq_card_labeled_div (P : Puzzle n) :

  rw [card_labeledAssembly, Nat.mul_div_cancel _ (by positivity)]

  have := h (a₁ := Sum.inl 0) (a₂ := Sum.inl 1) rfl

  have h1 : count P = 1 := by decide
  exact ⟨h1, (count_compPuzzle P).trans h1, even_card_labeledAssembly P,
    even_card_labeledAssembly _⟩

end JigsawParsimony",

/-!
# Parsimonious counting reductions: `#SAT → #Jigsaw → #Jigsaw`

We formalise a *counting problem* (instances, an encoding size, and a count) and a
*parsimonious reduction* between counting problems: an instance map preserving the
exact count and blowing up the encoding size at most linearly.  (Linear size
growth is the formal proxy used here for "polynomial-time"; the maps below are
structural recursions over lists, but running time itself is not modelled.)

## Main results

* `ParsimoniousReduction.comp`, `ParsimoniousReduction.count_modEq` : parsimonious
  reductions compose and transport every modular count (`⊕P`, `Mod_kP`).
* `compReduction` / `compPuzzle_isParsimoniousSelfReduction` : global complementation
  is a size-preserving, involutive parsimonious self-reduction of `#Jigsaw`.
* `count_toPuzzle` : the encoding of DIMACS CNF formulas as framed puzzles preserves
  the number of solutions exactly (literals naming undeclared variables are
  genuinely unsatisfiable on both sides), giving `satToJigsaw`.
* `toDimacs`, `satCount_toDimacs` : the converse encoding, so `#SAT` and `#Jigsaw` are
  parsimoniously inter-reducible; `satToJigsawComp` composes with complementation.
* `reduction_to_jigsaw_of_reduction_to_sat` : every counting problem that reduces
  parsimoniously to `#SAT` reduces parsimoniously to `#Jigsaw`, through either `P`
  or its complement.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace JigsawParsimony

open Finset

/-- A counting problem: instances with an encoding size and a solution count. -/
structure CountingProblem where
  Inst : Type
  size : Inst → ℕ
  count : Inst → ℕ

/-- A parsimonious reduction with linearly bounded size growth. -/
structure ParsimoniousReduction (A B : CountingProblem) where
  map : A.Inst → B.Inst
  count_map : ∀ x, B.count (map x) = A.count x
  sizeMul : ℕ
  sizeAdd : ℕ
  size_map : ∀ x, B.size (map x) ≤ sizeMul * A.size x + sizeAdd

namespace ParsimoniousReduction

variable {A B C : CountingProblem}

/-- The identity reduction. -/
def refl (A : CountingProblem) : ParsimoniousReduction A A :=
  ⟨id, fun _ => rfl, 1, 0, fun x => by simp⟩

/-- Composition of parsimonious reductions. -/
def comp (g : ParsimoniousReduction B C) (f : ParsimoniousReduction A B) :
    ParsimoniousReduction A C where
  map := g.map ∘ f.map
  count_map x := by simp [g.count_map, f.count_map]
  sizeMul := g.sizeMul * f.sizeMul
  sizeAdd := g.sizeMul * f.sizeAdd + g.sizeAdd
  size_map x := by
    have h1 := g.size_map (f.map x)
    have h2 := f.size_map x
    calc C.size (g.map (f.map x)) ≤ g.sizeMul * B.size (f.map x) + g.sizeAdd := h1
      _ ≤ g.sizeMul * (f.sizeMul * A.size x + f.sizeAdd) + g.sizeAdd := by gcongr
      _ = g.sizeMul * f.sizeMul * A.size x + (g.sizeMul * f.sizeAdd + g.sizeAdd) := by ring

/-- Parsimonious reductions transport every modular counting class. -/
theorem count_modEq (f : ParsimoniousReduction A B) (k : ℕ) (x : A.Inst) :
    B.count (f.map x) ≡ A.count x [MOD k] := by
  rw [f.count_map]

/-- In particular they transport the mod-2 count. -/
theorem even_count_iff (f : ParsimoniousReduction A B) (x : A.Inst) :
    Even (B.count (f.map x)) ↔ Even (A.count x) := by
  rw [f.count_map]

end ParsimoniousReduction

/-! ## The counting problem `#Jigsaw` and its complementation self-reduction -/

/-- Encoding size of a framed puzzle: sockets + literal inputs + clause pieces. -/
def puzzleSize {n : ℕ} (P : Puzzle n) : ℕ := n + (P.map List.length).sum + P.length

/-- The assembly counting problem for framed jigsaw puzzles. -/
def jigsawCount : CountingProblem where
  Inst := Σ n : ℕ, Puzzle n
  size x := puzzleSize x.2
  count x := count x.2

    puzzleSize (compPuzzle P) = puzzleSize P := by
  simp [puzzleSize, compPuzzle, Function.comp_def]

  map := compInst
  count_map x := count_compPuzzle x.2
  sizeMul := 1
  sizeAdd := 0

  rintro ⟨n, P⟩

/-- A self-map of an instance space is a *parsimonious self-reduction* if it
preserves the count and grows the size at most linearly. -/
def IsParsimoniousSelfReduction (A : CountingProblem) (f : A.Inst → A.Inst) : Prop :=
  (∀ x, A.count (f x) = A.count x) ∧ ∃ c d : ℕ, ∀ x, A.size (f x) ≤ c * A.size x + d

  ⟨compReduction.count_map, 1, 0, compReduction.size_map⟩

/-! ## `#SAT` in DIMACS format -/

/-- A CNF formula in DIMACS style: `nvars` declared variables, literals are nonzero
integers `±(i+1)`. -/
structure DimacsCNF where
  nvars : ℕ
  clauses : List (List ℤ)

/-- Polarity of a DIMACS literal as an element of `ZMod 2`. -/
def dimacsPol (k : ℤ) : ZMod 2 := if 0 < k then 1 else 0

/-- A DIMACS literal is true under `a` if it names a declared variable carrying the
right polarity.  Literals naming undeclared variables (or `0`) are false. -/
def DimacsLitTrue {nv : ℕ} (a : Cube nv) (k : ℤ) : Prop :=
  ∃ i : Fin nv, k.natAbs = i.1 + 1 ∧ a i = dimacsPol k

instance {nv : ℕ} (a : Cube nv) (k : ℤ) : Decidable (DimacsLitTrue a k) := by
  unfold DimacsLitTrue; infer_instance

/-- Satisfaction of a DIMACS formula. -/
def DimacsCNF.Sat (F : DimacsCNF) (a : Cube F.nvars) : Prop :=
  ∀ c ∈ F.clauses, ∃ k ∈ c, DimacsLitTrue a k

instance (F : DimacsCNF) : DecidablePred F.Sat := by
  intro a; unfold DimacsCNF.Sat; infer_instance

/-- The number of satisfying assignments of the declared variables. -/
def satCount (F : DimacsCNF) : ℕ := (univ.filter F.Sat).card

/-- Encoding size of a DIMACS formula. -/
def dimacsSize (F : DimacsCNF) : ℕ := F.nvars + (F.clauses.map List.length).sum + F.clauses.length

/-- The counting problem `#SAT`. -/
def sharpSAT : CountingProblem := ⟨DimacsCNF, dimacsSize, satCount⟩

/-- Translate a DIMACS literal into a literal input milled for a declared socket,
discarding literals that name no declared variable. -/
def toLit (nv : ℕ) (k : ℤ) : Option (Lit nv) :=
  if h : k.natAbs - 1 < nv ∧ k ≠ 0 then some (⟨k.natAbs - 1, h.1⟩, dimacsPol k) else none

/-- The puzzle built from a DIMACS formula: one clause piece per clause. -/
def toPuzzle (F : DimacsCNF) : Puzzle F.nvars :=
  F.clauses.map (List.filterMap (toLit F.nvars))

    (∃ l, toLit nv k = some l ∧ Fits a l) ↔ DimacsLitTrue a k := by
  unfold toLit DimacsLitTrue Fits
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨l, hl, hf⟩
    split_ifs at hl with h
    cases hl
    refine ⟨⟨k.natAbs - 1, h.1⟩, ?_, hf⟩
    have : k.natAbs ≠ 0 := Int.natAbs_ne_zero.2 h.2

  · rintro ⟨i, hi, ha⟩

    have : (⟨k.natAbs - 1, hlt⟩ : Fin nv) = i := Fin.ext (by simp only; omega)

/-- **Witness-level correspondence.**  An assignment assembles the encoded puzzle
iff it satisfies the formula. -/
theorem assembles_toPuzzle_iff (F : DimacsCNF) (a : Cube F.nvars) :
    Assembles (toPuzzle F) a ↔ F.Sat a := by
  unfold Assembles toPuzzle DimacsCNF.Sat
  constructor
  · intro h c hc

  · intro h c hc
    obtain ⟨c', hc', rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 hc
    exact (clausePiece_fits_iff a c').2 (h c' hc')

/-- **Parsimony of the SAT-to-puzzle encoding.** -/
theorem count_toPuzzle (F : DimacsCNF) : count (toPuzzle F) = satCount F := by
  unfold count assemblies satCount
  congr 1
  ext a
  simp [assembles_toPuzzle_iff]

  induction l with
  | nil => simp
  | cons x l ih =>

      split <;> simp <;> omega

  unfold puzzleSize dimacsSize toPuzzle
  simp only [List.map_map, List.length_map, add_le_add_iff_right, add_le_add_iff_left]
  apply List.sum_le_sum
  intro c _
  exact length_filterMap_le _ _

/-- The parsimonious reduction `#SAT → #Jigsaw`. -/
def satToJigsaw : ParsimoniousReduction sharpSAT jigsawCount where
  map F := ⟨F.nvars, toPuzzle F⟩
  count_map F := count_toPuzzle F
  sizeMul := 1
  sizeAdd := 0
  size_map F := by simpa [jigsawCount, sharpSAT] using puzzleSize_toPuzzle_le F

def satToJigsawComp : ParsimoniousReduction sharpSAT jigsawCount :=
  compReduction.comp satToJigsaw

/-!
# Parity-preserving self-reduction for jigsaw assembly counting — the model

A *framed jigsaw puzzle on `n` variables* consists of `n` variable sockets, each of
which receives one of two variable pieces (tab = `1`, blank = `0`), together with a
list of clause pieces.  A clause piece exposes finitely many literal inputs, each
milled for a socket `i : Fin n` and a polarity `p : ZMod 2`; it snaps into place iff
at least one of its inputs mates with the variable piece chosen at its socket.

We work over `ZMod 2` so that global tab–blank complementation becomes the
translation `p ↦ p + 1`, and the whole symmetry group of the instance space is the
*hyperoctahedral group* `(ZMod 2)^n ⋊ Sₙ` of signed permutations of the sockets.

## Main results

* `SignedPerm.assemblyEquiv` : every signed permutation `g` induces an explicit
  bijection between the assembly space of `P` and that of `g • P`.
* `SignedPerm.count_actPuzzle` : the assembly count is an invariant of the whole
  hyperoctahedral action (not only of global complementation).
* `SignedPerm.actPuzzle_mul` : the action on puzzles is compatible with the group
  law of signed permutations, so invariance holds along whole orbits.
* `count_compPuzzle`, `count_compPuzzle_modEq`, `even_count_compPuzzle_iff` :
  global complementation is parsimonious; in particular every modular count, and
  the mod-2 count, is a complementation invariant.
* `compPuzzle_eq_self_iff` : complementation acts *freely* on the instance space
  away from the degenerate puzzles all of whose clause pieces are empty.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace JigsawParsimony

open Finset

/-- The Boolean cube of variable-piece choices, written additively over `ZMod 2`. -/
abbrev Cube (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ZMod 2

/-- A literal input of a clause piece: a socket together with the polarity it is
milled for. -/
abbrev Lit (n : ℕ) := Fin n × ZMod 2

/-- A clause piece, given by its list of literal inputs. -/
abbrev ClausePiece (n : ℕ) := List (Lit n)

/-- A framed puzzle on `n` variables: its list of clause pieces. -/
abbrev Puzzle (n : ℕ) := List (ClausePiece n)

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- A literal input mates with the variable piece chosen at its socket. -/
def Fits (a : Cube n) (l : Lit n) : Prop := a l.1 = l.2

instance (a : Cube n) (l : Lit n) : Decidable (Fits a l) := by
  unfold Fits; infer_instance

/-- A choice of variable pieces assembles the puzzle when every clause piece has an
input that mates. -/
def Assembles (P : Puzzle n) (a : Cube n) : Prop := ∀ c ∈ P, ∃ l ∈ c, Fits a l

instance (P : Puzzle n) : DecidablePred (Assembles P) := by
  intro a; unfold Assembles; infer_instance

/-- The full (finite) assembly space of a puzzle. -/
def assemblies (P : Puzzle n) : Finset (Cube n) := univ.filter (Assembles P)

/-- The assembly count of a puzzle. -/
def count (P : Puzzle n) : ℕ := (assemblies P).card

@[simp] theorem mem_assemblies {P : Puzzle n} {a : Cube n} :
    a ∈ assemblies P ↔ Assembles P a := by
  simp [assemblies]

theorem count_eq_card_subtype (P : Puzzle n) :
    count P = Fintype.card {a : Cube n // Assembles P a} := by
  rw [Fintype.card_subtype]; rfl

/-! ## The hyperoctahedral group acting on puzzles -/

/-- A signed permutation of the sockets: relabel sockets by `perm`, then flip the
tab/blank polarity at socket `i` by `mask i`. -/
@[ext] structure SignedPerm (n : ℕ) where
  perm : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)
  mask : Cube n

namespace SignedPerm

variable (g h : SignedPerm n)

/-- Action on literal inputs. -/
def actLit (l : Lit n) : Lit n := (g.perm l.1, l.2 + g.mask l.1)

/-- Action on puzzles: transform every literal input of every clause piece. -/
def actPuzzle (P : Puzzle n) : Puzzle n := P.map (List.map g.actLit)

/-- Action on choices of variable pieces. -/
def actCube (a : Cube n) : Cube n := fun j => a (g.perm.symm j) + g.mask (g.perm.symm j)

/-- Inverse action on choices of variable pieces. -/
def invCube (b : Cube n) : Cube n := fun i => b (g.perm i) - g.mask i

theorem invCube_actCube (a : Cube n) : g.invCube (g.actCube a) = a := by
  funext i; simp [invCube, actCube]

theorem actCube_invCube (b : Cube n) : g.actCube (g.invCube b) = b := by
  funext j; simp [invCube, actCube]

theorem actCube_injective : Function.Injective g.actCube :=
  Function.LeftInverse.injective g.invCube_actCube

/-- Literal level transport. -/
theorem fits_act (a : Cube n) (l : Lit n) :
    Fits (g.actCube a) (g.actLit l) ↔ Fits a l := by
  simp only [Fits, actCube, actLit, Equiv.symm_apply_apply]
  exact add_left_inj _

/-- Puzzle level transport: `g` maps assemblies of `P` exactly onto assemblies of
`g • P`. -/
theorem assembles_act (P : Puzzle n) (a : Cube n) :
    Assembles (g.actPuzzle P) (g.actCube a) ↔ Assembles P a := by
  constructor
  · intro h c hc
    obtain ⟨l, hl, hf⟩ := h _ (List.mem_map_of_mem hc)
    obtain ⟨l', hl', rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 hl
    exact ⟨l', hl', (g.fits_act a l').1 hf⟩
  · intro h c hc
    obtain ⟨c', hc', rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 hc
    obtain ⟨l, hl, hf⟩ := h c' hc'
    exact ⟨g.actLit l, List.mem_map_of_mem hl, (g.fits_act a l).2 hf⟩

/-- **Witness-preserving bijection** induced by a signed permutation. -/
def assemblyEquiv (P : Puzzle n) :
    {a : Cube n // Assembles P a} ≃ {b : Cube n // Assembles (g.actPuzzle P) b} where
  toFun a := ⟨g.actCube a.1, (g.assembles_act P a.1).2 a.2⟩
  invFun b := ⟨g.invCube b.1, by
    have hb := b.2
    rw [← g.actCube_invCube b.1] at hb
    exact (g.assembles_act P _).1 hb⟩
  left_inv a := Subtype.ext (g.invCube_actCube a.1)
  right_inv b := Subtype.ext (g.actCube_invCube b.1)

/-- The assembly space of `g • P` is the image of that of `P`. -/
theorem assemblies_actPuzzle (P : Puzzle n) :
    assemblies (g.actPuzzle P) = (assemblies P).image g.actCube := by
  ext b
  simp only [mem_assemblies, Finset.mem_image]
  constructor
  · intro hb
    refine ⟨g.invCube b, ?_, g.actCube_invCube b⟩
    rw [← g.actCube_invCube b] at hb
    exact (g.assembles_act P _).1 hb
  · rintro ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩
    exact (g.assembles_act P a).2 ha

/-- **Hyperoctahedral invariance of the assembly count.** -/
theorem count_actPuzzle (P : Puzzle n) : count (g.actPuzzle P) = count P := by
  rw [count_eq_card_subtype, count_eq_card_subtype]
  exact (Fintype.card_congr (g.assemblyEquiv P)).symm

/-- Group law of signed permutations (`g * h` acts as "first `h`, then `g`"). -/
instance : Mul (SignedPerm n) :=
  ⟨fun g h => ⟨h.perm.trans g.perm, fun i => h.mask i + g.mask (h.perm i)⟩⟩

theorem mul_perm : (g * h).perm = h.perm.trans g.perm := rfl

theorem mul_mask (i : Fin n) : (g * h).mask i = h.mask i + g.mask (h.perm i) := rfl

theorem actLit_mul (l : Lit n) : (g * h).actLit l = g.actLit (h.actLit l) := by
  simp only [actLit, mul_perm, mul_mask, Equiv.trans_apply, Prod.mk.injEq, true_and]
  ring

/-- The action on puzzles is a genuine (left) action of the signed-permutation
monoid. -/
theorem actPuzzle_mul (P : Puzzle n) :
    (g * h).actPuzzle P = g.actPuzzle (h.actPuzzle P) := by
  simp only [actPuzzle, List.map_map]
  refine List.map_congr_left fun c _ => ?_
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, List.map_map]
  exact List.map_congr_left fun l _ => g.actLit_mul h l

/-- Orbit invariance: the count is constant along any finite word of signed
permutations. -/
theorem count_foldr_actPuzzle (gs : List (SignedPerm n)) (P : Puzzle n) :
    count (gs.foldr (fun g Q => g.actPuzzle Q) P) = count P := by
  induction gs with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons g gs ih => simp only [List.foldr_cons]; rw [count_actPuzzle, ih]

end SignedPerm

/-! ## Global tab–blank complementation -/

/-- Global complementation of a puzzle: reverse the polarity of every literal
input. -/
def compPuzzle (P : Puzzle n) : Puzzle n := P.map (List.map fun l => (l.1, l.2 + 1))

/-- Global complementation of a choice of variable pieces. -/
def compCube (a : Cube n) : Cube n := fun i => a i + 1

/-- Complementation is the signed permutation with trivial relabelling and full
mask. -/
def compSigned (n : ℕ) : SignedPerm n := ⟨1, fun _ => 1⟩

theorem compPuzzle_eq_actPuzzle (P : Puzzle n) :
    compPuzzle P = (compSigned n).actPuzzle P := rfl

theorem compCube_eq_actCube (a : Cube n) : compCube a = (compSigned n).actCube a := rfl

theorem add_one_add_one_zmod2 (x : ZMod 2) : x + 1 + 1 = x := by
  rw [add_assoc]; fin_cases x <;> rfl

theorem compPuzzle_involutive : Function.Involutive (compPuzzle (n := n)) := by
  intro P
  simp only [compPuzzle, List.map_map]
  conv_rhs => rw [← List.map_id P]
  refine List.map_congr_left fun c _ => ?_
  simp only [Function.comp_apply, List.map_map, id]
  conv_rhs => rw [← List.map_id c]
  refine List.map_congr_left fun l _ => ?_
  simp [add_one_add_one_zmod2]

theorem compCube_involutive : Function.Involutive (compCube (n := n)) := by
  intro a; funext i; simp [compCube, add_one_add_one_zmod2]

/-- The witness-preserving complementation bijection `assemblyEquiv`. -/
def assemblyEquiv (P : Puzzle n) :
    {a : Cube n // Assembles P a} ≃ {b : Cube n // Assembles (compPuzzle P) b} :=
  (compSigned n).assemblyEquiv P

/-- **Parsimony of complementation.**  `P` and its complement have equal assembly
counts. -/
theorem count_compPuzzle (P : Puzzle n) : count (compPuzzle P) = count P :=
  (compSigned n).count_actPuzzle P

/-- Every modular counting class is a complementation invariant. -/
theorem count_compPuzzle_modEq (k : ℕ) (P : Puzzle n) :
    count (compPuzzle P) ≡ count P [MOD k] := by
  rw [count_compPuzzle]

/-- The mod-2 assembly count is a complementation invariant. -/
theorem even_count_compPuzzle_iff (P : Puzzle n) :
    Even (count (compPuzzle P)) ↔ Even (count P) := by
  rw [count_compPuzzle]

/-- A clause piece is fixed by complementation only if it has no inputs. -/
theorem compClause_eq_self_iff (c : ClausePiece n) :
    c.map (fun l => (l.1, l.2 + 1)) = c ↔ c = [] := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    cases c with
    | nil => rfl
    | cons l c =>
        exfalso
        have h1 := (List.cons.inj h).1
        have h2 : l.2 + 1 = l.2 := congrArg Prod.snd h1
        have : (1 : ZMod 2) = 0 := by
          have := congrArg (fun x => x - l.2) h2
          simp at this
        exact absurd this (by decide)
  · rintro rfl; rfl

/-- **Freeness on the instance space.**  A puzzle is its own complement exactly
when all its clause pieces are empty; on every other instance complementation
moves the instance. -/

    return (perm, mask)

concept.title: Multi-window crossing law
concept.concept_description:
**Conjecture.** Suppose an oracle names \(k\) nested windows \(w_1 < \dots < w_k\) with cumulative reliabilities \(\alpha_1 < \dots < \alpha_k\). Under stipulated pricing, speedup \(s\) is reachable iff \(\sum_i (\alpha_i - \alpha_{i-1})\,\cdot\) (mean slot of block \(i\)) is at most \(1/(3s)\). This is a polyhedral gate whose single-window case is `crossing_law`.
The key insight is that the displacement law extends to step posteriors: the cost of an order is a sum of the block-weight jumps times the index sums of the upper sets.
Why now? `displacement_law` and `exchange_sum_le` already give the single-step case.

  have : ∑ j ∈ range M, ((j : ℝ) + 1) * (if B i ≤ j ∧ j < B (i + 1) then blockDensity B A i
      else 0) = blockDensity B A i * ∑ j ∈ Ico (B i) (B (i + 1)), ((j : ℝ) + 1) := by
    rw [← hfilt, sum_filter, mul_sum]
    exact sum_congr rfl fun j _ => by split_ifs <;> ring
  rw [this, sum_Ico_succ_real _ _ hlt.le]
  unfold blockDensity
  have hne : (B (i + 1) : ℝ) - B i ≠ 0 := by
    have : (B i : ℝ) < B (i + 1) := by exact_mod_cast hlt
    linarith
  field_simp

/-- The **gate functional** `Φ(x, A) = Σ_i (A(i+1) - A i) · (x i + x (i+1)) / 2`: block mass
times the mean normalized slot of the block. -/
noncomputable def gateCost (n : ℕ) (x A : ℕ → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i ∈ range n, (A (i + 1) - A i) * ((x i + x (i + 1)) / 2)

lemma sum_range_telescope (n : ℕ) (f : ℕ → ℝ) : ∑ i ∈ range n, (f (i + 1) - f i) = f n - f 0 :=
  sum_range_sub f n

/-- **Normalized committed cost.**  With `x i = B i / M`, the committed cost is exactly
`M · Φ(x, A) + (A n - A 0)/2`. -/
theorem committed_cost_normalized (M n : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) (B : ℕ → ℕ) (A : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hB : StrictMono B) (hBn : B n ≤ M) :
    probeCost (stepPosterior (M := M) n B A) (Equiv.refl _) =
      M * gateCost n (fun i => (B i : ℝ) / M) A + (A n - A 0) / 2 := by
  rw [committed_cost_blocks M n B A hB hBn, gateCost, ← sum_range_telescope n A, mul_sum,
    sum_div, ← sum_add_distrib]
  have hM' : (M : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hM.ne'
  refine sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
  field_simp

/-! ## 2. Calibrated step posteriors: Bayes ≡ Committed -/

lemma stepWeight_on_block (n : ℕ) (B : ℕ → ℕ) (A : ℕ → ℝ) (hB : StrictMono B) (i j : ℕ)
    (hi : i < n) (h1 : B i ≤ j) (h2 : j < B (i + 1)) :
    stepWeight n B A j = blockDensity B A i := by
  unfold stepWeight
  rw [sum_eq_single i]
  · rw [if_pos ⟨h1, h2⟩]
  · intro l _ hli
    rw [if_neg]
    rintro ⟨hl1, hl2⟩
    rcases Nat.lt_or_gt_of_ne hli with h | h
    · have := hB.monotone (show l + 1 ≤ i by omega); omega
    · have := hB.monotone (show i + 1 ≤ l by omega); omega
  · intro h; exact absurd (mem_range.2 hi) h

lemma exists_block (n : ℕ) (B : ℕ → ℕ) (hB0 : B 0 = 0) (j : ℕ) (hj : j < B n) :
    ∃ i, i < n ∧ B i ≤ j ∧ j < B (i + 1) := by
  have hn : n ≠ 0 := by rintro rfl; omega
  have hex : ∃ i, j < B (i + 1) := ⟨n - 1, by rw [Nat.sub_add_cancel (by omega)]; exact hj⟩
  classical
  refine ⟨Nat.find hex, ?_, ?_, Nat.find_spec hex⟩
  · have := Nat.find_min' hex (show j < B (n - 1 + 1) by rw [Nat.sub_add_cancel (by omega)]; exact hj)
    omega
  · rcases h : Nat.find hex with _ | m
    · rw [hB0]; omega
    · have := Nat.find_min hex (show m < Nat.find hex by omega)
      omega

/-- **Calibrated step posteriors are nonincreasing.**  If the block densities are
nonincreasing, so is the step posterior on `Fin (B n)`. -/
theorem stepPosterior_antitone (n : ℕ) (B : ℕ → ℕ) (A : ℕ → ℝ) (hB : StrictMono B)
    (hB0 : B 0 = 0) (hd : AntitoneOn (blockDensity B A) (Set.Iio n)) :
    Antitone (stepPosterior (M := B n) n B A) := by
  intro j j' hjj'
  obtain ⟨i, hi, hi1, hi2⟩ := exists_block n B hB0 j j.isLt
  obtain ⟨i', hi', hi1', hi2'⟩ := exists_block n B hB0 j' j'.isLt
  have hjj : (j : ℕ) ≤ j' := hjj'
  have hii : i ≤ i' := by
    by_contra h
    have := hB.monotone (show i' + 1 ≤ i by omega)
    omega
  unfold stepPosterior
  rw [stepWeight_on_block n B A hB i j hi hi1 hi2, stepWeight_on_block n B A hB i' j' hi' hi1' hi2']
  exact hd (Set.mem_Iio.2 hi) (Set.mem_Iio.2 hi') hii

/-- **Bayes ≡ Committed for calibrated nested windows.**  If the block densities are
nonincreasing, committed search is optimal among all orders of the `M = B n` cells. -/
theorem multi_window_bayes_optimal (n : ℕ) (B : ℕ → ℕ) (A : ℕ → ℝ) (hB : StrictMono B)
    (hB0 : B 0 = 0) (hd : AntitoneOn (blockDensity B A) (Set.Iio n))
    (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin (B n))) :
    probeCost (stepPosterior (M := B n) n B A) (Equiv.refl _) ≤
      probeCost (stepPosterior (M := B n) n B A) σ := by
  have hanti := stepPosterior_antitone n B A hB hB0 hd
  generalize hM : B n = M at σ hanti ⊢
  rcases M with _ | N
  · unfold probeCost; simp
  · exact committed_optimal_of_antitone N _ hanti σ

/-! ## 3. The exact multi-window crossing law -/

/-- The stipulated blind price: the min-law blind cost `(M+1)(2M+1)/(6M)`. -/
noncomputable def minBlind (M : ℕ) : ℝ := ((M : ℝ) + 1) * (2 * M + 1) / (6 * M)

/-- **Exact multi-window crossing law.**  For calibrated nested windows (`B 0 = 0`,
nonincreasing block densities, `A 0 = 0`, `A n = 1`) on `M = B n > 0` cells, speedup `s` is
reachable by **some** search order iff the gate functional satisfies
`s · (M · Φ(B/M, A) + 1/2) ≤ minBlind M`. -/
theorem multi_window_crossing_law_exact (n : ℕ) (B : ℕ → ℕ) (A : ℕ → ℝ) (hB : StrictMono B)
    (hB0 : B 0 = 0) (hM : 0 < B n) (hA0 : A 0 = 0) (hAn : A n = 1)
    (hd : AntitoneOn (blockDensity B A) (Set.Iio n)) (s : ℝ) (hs : 0 < s) :
    (∃ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin (B n)),
        s * probeCost (stepPosterior (M := B n) n B A) σ ≤ minBlind (B n)) ↔
      s * ((B n : ℝ) * gateCost n (fun i => (B i : ℝ) / B n) A + 1 / 2) ≤ minBlind (B n) := by
  have hc := committed_cost_normalized (B n) n hM B A hB le_rfl
  rw [hA0, hAn] at hc
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨σ, hσ⟩
    have hopt := multi_window_bayes_optimal n B A hB hB0 hd σ
    rw [hc] at hopt
    have : s * ((B n : ℝ) * gateCost n (fun i => (B i : ℝ) / B n) A + (1 - 0) / 2) ≤
        s * probeCost (stepPosterior (M := B n) n B A) σ :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hopt hs.le
    norm_num at this ⊢
    linarith
  · intro h
    refine ⟨Equiv.refl _, ?_⟩
    rw [hc]; norm_num at h ⊢; linarith

/-! ## 4. The continuum gate -/

/-- Continuum priced speedup: blind cost `1/3` (per cell) against `Φ`. -/
noncomputable def multiSpeedup (n : ℕ) (x A : ℕ → ℝ) : ℝ := 1 / (3 * gateCost n x A)

/-- **THE MULTI-WINDOW CROSSING LAW (continuum).**  Speedup `s` is reachable iff
`Σ_i (A(i+1) - A i) · (mean slot of block i) ≤ 1/(3s)`. -/
theorem multi_crossing_law (n : ℕ) (x A : ℕ → ℝ) (s : ℝ) (hs : 0 < s)
    (hpos : 0 < gateCost n x A) :
    s ≤ multiSpeedup n x A ↔ gateCost n x A ≤ 1 / (3 * s) := by
  unfold multiSpeedup
  rw [le_div_iff₀ (by positivity), le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)]
  constructor <;> intro h <;> linarith

/-- Area under the piecewise-linear reliability curve through the points `(x i, A i)`. -/
noncomputable def reliabilityArea (n : ℕ) (x A : ℕ → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i ∈ range n, ((A i + A (i + 1)) / 2) * (x (i + 1) - x i)

/-- **Gate functional + area = boundary term** (summation by parts). -/
theorem gateCost_add_area (n : ℕ) (x A : ℕ → ℝ) :
    gateCost n x A + reliabilityArea n x A = A n * x n - A 0 * x 0 := by
  unfold gateCost reliabilityArea
  rw [← sum_add_distrib, ← sum_range_telescope n (fun i => A i * x i)]
  exact sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by ring

/-- **AUC form of the crossing law.**  On the normalized cell range `[0, 1]` with total
reliability `1`, speedup `s` is reachable iff the area under the reliability curve is at least
`1 - 1/(3s)`. -/
theorem auc_crossing_law (n : ℕ) (x A : ℕ → ℝ) (hx0 : x 0 = 0) (hxn : x n = 1) (hAn : A n = 1)
    (s : ℝ) (hs : 0 < s) (hpos : 0 < gateCost n x A) :
    s ≤ multiSpeedup n x A ↔ 1 - 1 / (3 * s) ≤ reliabilityArea n x A := by
  rw [multi_crossing_law n x A s hs hpos]
  have := gateCost_add_area n x A
  rw [hx0, hxn, hAn] at this
  constructor <;> intro h <;> linarith

/-- The single-window reliability gate `α_min(s) = 1 - 2/(3s)`. -/
noncomputable def alphaMin (s : ℝ) : ℝ := 1 - 2 / (3 * s)

/-- Single-window profile: points `(0,0)`, `(w, α)`, `(1,1)`. -/
noncomputable def singleX (w : ℝ) : ℕ → ℝ := fun i => if i = 0 then 0 else if i = 1 then w else 1
noncomputable def singleA (α : ℝ) : ℕ → ℝ := fun i => if i = 0 then 0 else if i = 1 then α else 1

lemma gateCost_single (α w : ℝ) : gateCost 2 (singleX w) (singleA α) = (1 - α + w) / 2 := by
  simp [gateCost, sum_range_succ, singleX, singleA]; ring

/-- **The single-window case is the crossing law.**  For `n = 2` the multi-window gate reads
`w ≤ α - α_min(s)`. -/
theorem single_window_crossing_law (s α w : ℝ) (hs : 0 < s) (hpos : 0 < 1 - α + w) :
    s ≤ multiSpeedup 2 (singleX w) (singleA α) ↔ w ≤ α - alphaMin s := by
  rw [multi_crossing_law 2 _ _ s hs (by rw [gateCost_single]; linarith), gateCost_single,
    alphaMin]
  have h : 2 / (3 * s) = 2 * (1 / (3 * s)) := by ring
  rw [h]
  constructor <;> intro h <;> linarith

/-- **Outer reliability gate.**  For a monotone profile (`0 = x 0 ≤ x 1 ≤ … ≤ x n = 1`,
`A` nondecreasing, `A n = 1`, `n ≥ 1`), reaching speedup `s` forces
`(1 - A (n-1)) (1 + x (n-1)) ≤ 2/(3s)`; in particular, if the widest window has positive width,
its reliability must exceed `α_min(s)` — no number of inner windows can substitute. -/
theorem outer_reliability_gate (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (x A : ℕ → ℝ) (hx0 : x 0 = 0)
    (hxm : Monotone x) (hxn : x n = 1) (hAm : Monotone A) (hAn : A n = 1) (s : ℝ) (hs : 0 < s)
    (hpos : 0 < gateCost n x A) (hreach : s ≤ multiSpeedup n x A) (hw : 0 < x (n - 1)) :
    alphaMin s < A (n - 1) := by
  rw [multi_crossing_law n x A s hs hpos] at hreach
  obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ : ∃ m, n = m + 1 := ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩
  simp only [Nat.add_sub_cancel] at hw ⊢
  have hlast : (1 - A m) * ((x m + 1) / 2) ≤ gateCost (m + 1) x A := by
    unfold gateCost
    rw [sum_range_succ, hAn, hxn]
    have : 0 ≤ ∑ i ∈ range m, (A (i + 1) - A i) * ((x i + x (i + 1)) / 2) := by
      refine sum_nonneg fun i _ => mul_nonneg (by linarith [hAm (Nat.le_succ i)]) ?_
      have := hxm (Nat.zero_le i); have := hxm (Nat.zero_le (i + 1)); linarith
    linarith
  have hA1 : A m ≤ 1 := by rw [← hAn]; exact hAm (Nat.le_succ m)
  unfold alphaMin
  have h3 : 1 / (3 * s) * 2 = 2 / (3 * s) := by ring
  rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hA1 with h | h
  · rw [h]; have : 0 < 2 / (3 * s) := by positivity
    linarith
  · have hprod : (1 - A m) * (x m + 1) ≤ 2 / (3 * s) := by linarith
    have : (1 - A m) * 1 < (1 - A m) * (x m + 1) := mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left (by linarith)
      (by linarith)
    linarith

/-! ## 5. Refinement, monotonicity and convexity of the gate -/

/-- **Refinement identity.**  Splitting the block `(x_l, a_l) → (x_r, a_r)` at the new window
point `(x', α')` changes the gate functional by `-(x_r - x_l)(α' - chord(x'))/2`, where
`(x_r - x_l) · chord(x') = a_l (x_r - x') + a_r (x' - x_l)`. -/
theorem refinement_identity (xl xr x' al ar α' : ℝ) :
    ((α' - al) * ((xl + x') / 2) + (ar - α') * ((x' + xr) / 2)) - (ar - al) * ((xl + xr) / 2) =
      -((xr - xl) * α' - (al * (xr - x') + ar * (x' - xl))) / 2 := by
  ring

/-- **A new window helps iff it lies strictly above the chord.** -/
theorem refinement_helps_iff (xl xr x' al ar α' : ℝ) :
    (α' - al) * ((xl + x') / 2) + (ar - α') * ((x' + xr) / 2) < (ar - al) * ((xl + xr) / 2) ↔
      al * (xr - x') + ar * (x' - xl) < (xr - xl) * α' := by
  have := refinement_identity xl xr x' al ar α'
  constructor <;> intro h <;> linarith

/-- The gate functional is affine (indeed linear) in the reliability profile. -/
theorem gateCost_affine (n : ℕ) (x A A' : ℕ → ℝ) (t : ℝ) :
    gateCost n x (fun i => t * A i + (1 - t) * A' i) =
      t * gateCost n x A + (1 - t) * gateCost n x A' := by
  unfold gateCost
  rw [mul_sum, mul_sum, ← sum_add_distrib]
  exact sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by ring

/-- **The gate is convex (polyhedral) in the reliabilities.**  If two reliability profiles
on the same windows both satisfy the gate `Φ ≤ 1/(3s)`, so does every mixture. -/
theorem gate_convex (n : ℕ) (x A A' : ℕ → ℝ) (s t : ℝ) (ht0 : 0 ≤ t) (ht1 : t ≤ 1)
    (hA : gateCost n x A ≤ 1 / (3 * s)) (hA' : gateCost n x A' ≤ 1 / (3 * s)) :
    gateCost n x (fun i => t * A i + (1 - t) * A' i) ≤ 1 / (3 * s) := by
  rw [gateCost_affine]
  nlinarith

/-- Coefficient form: `Φ = boundary - Σ_{inner} A i · (x (i+1) - x (i-1))/2`.  Raising an inner
reliability `A j` (`0 < j < n`) by `δ` lowers `Φ` by `δ (x (j+1) - x (j-1))/2`. -/
theorem gateCost_mono_reliability (n j : ℕ) (hj0 : 0 < j) (hjn : j < n) (x A : ℕ → ℝ)
    (δ : ℝ) :
    gateCost n x (Function.update A j (A j + δ)) =
      gateCost n x A - δ * (x (j + 1) - x (j - 1)) / 2 := by
  obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ : ∃ m, j = m + 1 := ⟨j - 1, by omega⟩
  have key : ∀ N, m + 2 ≤ N → gateCost N x (Function.update A (m + 1) (A (m + 1) + δ)) =
      gateCost N x A - δ * (x (m + 1 + 1) - x (m + 1 - 1)) / 2 := by
    intro N hN
    induction N, hN using Nat.le_induction with
    | base =>
      unfold gateCost
      rw [sum_range_succ, sum_range_succ, sum_range_succ, sum_range_succ]
      have hr : ∀ i ∈ range m, (Function.update A (m + 1) (A (m + 1) + δ) (i + 1) -
          Function.update A (m + 1) (A (m + 1) + δ) i) * ((x i + x (i + 1)) / 2) =
          (A (i + 1) - A i) * ((x i + x (i + 1)) / 2) := by
        intro i hi
        simp only [mem_range] at hi
        rw [Function.update_of_ne (by omega), Function.update_of_ne (by omega)]
      rw [sum_congr rfl hr]
      simp only [Function.update_self, Function.update_of_ne (show m ≠ m + 1 by omega),
        Function.update_of_ne (show m + 1 + 1 ≠ m + 1 by omega), Nat.add_sub_cancel]
      ring
    | succ N hN ih =>
      unfold gateCost at ih ⊢
      rw [sum_range_succ, sum_range_succ, ih,
        Function.update_of_ne (show N + 1 ≠ m + 1 by omega),
        Function.update_of_ne (show N ≠ m + 1 by omega)]
      ring
  exact key n (by omega)

/-- Widening an inner window `x j` (`0 < j < n`) by `δ`, at fixed cumulative reliabilities,
raises `Φ` by `δ (A (j+1) - A (j-1))/2 ≥ 0`: width never substitutes for reliability. -/
theorem gateCost_mono_width (n j : ℕ) (hj0 : 0 < j) (hjn : j < n) (x A : ℕ → ℝ) (δ : ℝ) :
    gateCost n (Function.update x j (x j + δ)) A =
      gateCost n x A + δ * (A (j + 1) - A (j - 1)) / 2 := by
  obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ : ∃ m, j = m + 1 := ⟨j - 1, by omega⟩
  have key : ∀ N, m + 2 ≤ N → gateCost N (Function.update x (m + 1) (x (m + 1) + δ)) A =
      gateCost N x A + δ * (A (m + 1 + 1) - A (m + 1 - 1)) / 2 := by
    intro N hN
    induction N, hN using Nat.le_induction with
    | base =>
      unfold gateCost
      rw [sum_range_succ, sum_range_succ, sum_range_succ, sum_range_succ]
      have hr : ∀ i ∈ range m, (A (i + 1) - A i) *
          ((Function.update x (m + 1) (x (m + 1) + δ) i +
            Function.update x (m + 1) (x (m + 1) + δ) (i + 1)) / 2) =
          (A (i + 1) - A i) * ((x i + x (i + 1)) / 2) := by
        intro i hi
        simp only [mem_range] at hi
        rw [Function.update_of_ne (by omega), Function.update_of_ne (by omega)]
      rw [sum_congr rfl hr]
      simp only [Function.update_self, Function.update_of_ne (show m ≠ m + 1 by omega),
        Function.update_of_ne (show m + 1 + 1 ≠ m + 1 by omega), Nat.add_sub_cancel]
      ring
    | succ N hN ih =>
      unfold gateCost at ih ⊢
      rw [sum_range_succ, sum_range_succ, ih,
        Function.update_of_ne (show N + 1 ≠ m + 1 by omega),
        Function.update_of_ne (show N ≠ m + 1 by omega)]
      ring
  exact key n (by omega)

/-! ## 6. The complement block cannot be dropped -/

/-- **The naive gate (windows only, no complement block) is false.**  For one window of width
`1/2` and reliability `1/2`, the windows-only sum `α · w/2 = 1/8` is below `1/(3·2) = 1/6`,
yet the true priced speedup is `2/3 < 2`. -/
theorem naive_gate_fails :
    let α : ℝ := 1 / 2
    let w : ℝ := 1 / 2
    (α - 0) * ((0 + w) / 2) ≤ 1 / (3 * 2) ∧
      multiSpeedup 2 (singleX w) (singleA α) < 2 := by
  intro α w
  refine ⟨by norm_num [α, w], ?_⟩
  unfold multiSpeedup
  rw [gateCost_single]
  norm_num [α, w]

end MultiWindowCrossingLaw
